$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Adopt one of the two presentations of the framework's field law, that is,
[[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]] or
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]], for a model with geometric data and matter
sector satisfying [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
and curvature tensors $R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$,
$G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let $T$ be the model's smooth
symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the matter domain
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]), let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the
constant parameter and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ as in
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be the
model's open matter domain and suppose the field law holds on $U$,

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U .$$

**(a) Necessary conservation.** $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $U$. Consequently a
prescribed smooth symmetric $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}\neq0$ at some point cannot
satisfy the field law there with that proposed metric; the divergence is
computed using its metric-selected connection, and may change if the metric
is changed.

**(b) Trace.** On $U$, $g^{ab}T_{ab}$ satisfies
$-S+4\Lambda=\kappa\,g^{ab}T_{ab}$.

**(c) Parameter variation.** If instead $\Lambda:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth
function and the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds on $U$
with that function in place of a constant, then on $U$

$$\kappa\nabla^aT_{ab}=\partial_b\Lambda .$$

Consequently, at every point where $d\Lambda\ne0$, the equation requires
$\nabla^aT_{ab}\ne0$; where $d\Lambda=0$, this identity imposes conservation.
A smooth $\Lambda$ can be locally constant but nonconstant across disconnected
components of $U$, in which case this identity does not force nonconservation.

**(d) A vacuum solution.** In the global vacuum example take
$U=M=\mathbb R^4$ with the identity chart and the flat metric
$g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ (a smooth Lorentzian metric
with time orientation $N=\partial_0$), the field law with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$
holds: $G=0$ and $S=0$ for the flat metric. With $T=0$ and $\Lambda\neq0$ it
fails, since $G+\Lambda g=\Lambda g\neq0$.

**(e) Energy conditions are additional assumptions.** Neither adopted
presentation of the field law contains a clause imposing any of the weak, null,
dominant or strong energy conditions of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]]; none of
the four is a universal consequence of that equation, as the direct-equation
perfect-fluid model in the proof shows. Particular matter models may imply
energy conditions; when not derived, they are additional assumptions in the
sense of clause (iv) of [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]].

**(f) Perfect-fluid rest-frame reading.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a
perfect-fluid model on its matter domain
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]), and at any $p\in U$ let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n_p$. Then
$T_{AB}=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,p,p,p)$ in that basis, and at $p$

$$T\ \text{satisfies WEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies NEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+p\ge0,\qquad T\ \text{satisfies DEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge|p|,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies SEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+3p\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0 .$$

In particular a model with $\varepsilon>0$ and $p=-\varepsilon$ satisfies the
NEC, WEC and DEC and violates the SEC; the inequality signs here are those of
the strict-timelike convention of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]], under which
continuity extensions to the causal cone are not assumed.

Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, and let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and curvature
$R$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). All statements below
are deductions within the model so specified; they assert nothing about
nature.

At an event $q$, a **frame** means an ordered basis
$(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ of $T_qM$. If an orthonormal frame is intended, it means
a tetrad satisfying $g_q(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$;
these terms and their distinction from coordinate frames are defined in
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. Such a frame is pointwise basis
data, not a chart on an open set or an observer congruence, which is a smooth
future unit timelike vector field on an open set
([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).

**(a) Free-fall congruences.** A **free-fall congruence** of the model is a
smooth map $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times I\to M$, with
$\varepsilon>0$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior,
whose values we write $\gamma(r,s)$. For each
$r\in(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ the curve $\gamma_r:I\to M$ is defined by
$\gamma_r(s):=\gamma(r,s)$ and is a future timelike geodesic parametrized by
proper time, with tangent field $U_r(s):=\partial_s\gamma(r,s)$ satisfying
$$g(U_r,U_r)=-c^2,\qquad D_sU_r=0,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$.
By clause (ii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], each $\gamma_r$ is
a worldline the model assigns to an ideal freely falling massive test body
with the corresponding release data, and conversely every such worldline
arises this way on its parameter interval. No injectivity or immersion
condition is imposed on the family map.

**(b) Deviation equation (model deduction).** Let $\gamma$ be a free-fall
congruence and set $J:=\partial_r\gamma$. Then, along each $\gamma_r$, the
separation field satisfies
$$D_s^2J=R(U_r,J)U_r,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$. In particular, the
relative four-acceleration encoded by the family’s infinitesimal separation
field $J$ is exactly the curvature term: at each event,
$J\mapsto R(U_r,J)U_r$ is an $\mathbb R$-linear map on the event's tangent
space, vanishes at $J=0$, is tensorial and independent of the frame or chart
used for its components, and contains no rest mass, charge or
internal-structure parameter of the bodies.

**(c) Flat comparison and the vanishing criterion.** If the curvature
vanishes on an open subset $O\subseteq M$, then every free-fall congruence
with worldlines in $O$ has $D_s^2J=0$ there: the model predicts no tidal
relative acceleration of freely falling test bodies in that region.
Conversely, if at an event $q$ the operator $J\mapsto R(U,J)U$ vanishes for
every future timelike $U$ and every $J\in T_qM$, then $R_q=0$; hence within
the model the tidal response of all free-fall congruences detects exactly the
curvature, and $R$ is the model's complete tidal field at every event.

**Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the stated
postulates and the cited mathematics. No observation, apparatus, measured
input or statistical inference is used; the item contains no empirical
premises, and the word "tidal" denotes the curvature term in the model's
deviation equation, not a measured force on any particular body.

derivations.claim: (The model and its field law.) By [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] clauses (a)-(c), $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold without boundary; by [A1] it satisfies the spacetime postulate, and $T=0$ is a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on the matter domain $M$. By [L1], $G_{ab}\equiv0$; with $\Lambda=0$ and $T=0$, $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=0=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds identically, and $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ trivially, so the prescription is admissible by [A1] and the field law holds by [A2]; this is also the flat vacuum solution of [L2]. This proves (a).

(Free fall and clock readings.) Let $p,U_0$ be as in (b), and write $U_0=c v$ with $\eta(v,v)=-1$, $v^0>0$; the normalization is possible by [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] clause (c). By [A3] the physical worldline is a restriction of the unique maximal future timelike geodesic through $(p,U_0)$, with proper time as affine parameter. By [L1] this maximal mathematical geodesic is the straight line $x(\gamma(s))=x_0+sv$. With proper-time parametrization $\tau=s/c$ (the normalization $\lambda=1$ of [L1]), this is $x(\gamma(\tau))=x_0+c\tau v$; the coordinate velocity is the constant $w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ with $|w|<c$ by [L1]. Finally, for two coordinate times in the physical domain, the ideal clock reads proper time by [A3], and from the parametrization $t=x^0/c$ along the line, $\Delta t=v^0\Delta\tau$; since $|w|^2/c^2=1-1/(v^0)^2$ by [L1] clause (e), $\sqrt{1-|w|^2/c^2}=1/v^0$ and hence $\Delta\tau=(1/v^0)(t_1-t_0)=\sqrt{1-|w|^2/c^2}(t_1-t_0)$. This proves (b).
(No tidal response.) The curvature vanishes identically by [L1], so by [L3] every free-fall congruence satisfies $D_\tau^2J=0$. This proves (c).

(Conclusion and status.) Steps 1.1-1.3 establish (a)-(c) as consequences of the adopted postulates and the cited mathematics, using no observation, apparatus or measured input; clause (d) records that the model is one solution among many and carries no empirical assertion, in particular no claim that the vacuum or the flat topology is realized in nature.

boundaries.reason: The model M is a nonempty four-manifold and the vacuum prescription T = 0 is a global field; no empty family or sum arises.

boundaries.evidence: statement clause (a) takes Λ = 0 and T = 0 and verifies G_ab = 0 identically by the vanishing curvature of the flat model; the zero parameter cases of the field law are the content of the model.

boundaries.reason: The dimension is four and no one-parameter specialization of the field law is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: statement clause (b) parametrizes worldlines by proper time using g(U0,U0) = -c², so the null and zero-velocity degenerate cases are excluded from the free-fall clause by hypothesis rather than silently assumed.
statement clause (b) integrates the clock reading between two coordinate times t0 < t1 and uses the maximal geodesic defined on all of ℝ, so both time endpoints are covered.

boundaries.reason: The event p and the four-velocity U0 are given data; the worldline is determined by them, and no selection occurs in the deduction.
The item asserts a conditional model statement and identities, not an equivalence.
No converse (for example that every vacuum solution is the flat model) is asserted; clause (d) explicitly states that other solutions are not excluded.

Free-fall/clock postulate gives physical restriction of unique maximal mathematical geodesic, avoiding an assertion of maximal physical lifetime. Normalized U0=cv yields x=x0+c tau v, w<c and Delta tau=Delta t/v0. Curvature-zero Jacobi response is conditional on congruence supplier. No measurements or empirical proof. citations.quote:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Let $(M,g_\eta,N_\eta)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and constant components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be a
nonempty open spacetime region, identified with its image in $\mathbb R^4$,
and let $\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be the spatial projection
$\pi(x^0,\mathbf x)=\mathbf x$. Its image $U:=\pi(\Omega)$ is open: a
coordinate ball in $\Omega$ about any point projects onto a ball about that
point's spatial coordinates. Let $K\subseteq U$ be compact. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N>0$ be the constants of the framework's conventions and put
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The coordinates have units of metres, $c$ has units
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ is dimensionless.

**(a) Structural data.** A tuple $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is
**stationary weak-field data** when

- $L>0$ is a length, $C>0$ is dimensionless, and $\varepsilon_0>0$ is
  dimensionless;
- $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth dimensionless spatial function and
  $r=(r_{ab})$ is a family of smooth dimensionless spatial functions
  $r_{ab}:(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times U\to\mathbb R$ for some
  $\varepsilon_1>\varepsilon_0$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]);
- for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)=\begin{cases}-(1+2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))+r_{00}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=b=0,\\[2pt] r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&\{a,b\}=\{0,i\},\\[2pt] (1-2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))\,\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=i,\ b=j,\end{cases}$$

  is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\varepsilon)$ on
  $\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
- **(spatial factorization and stationarity)** all metric components factor
  through $\pi$ by construction. Thus points of $\Omega$ with the same
  spatial coordinates have the same metric components, even when they lie in
  different connected components of that spatial fiber, and
  $\partial_0g_{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$;
- **(spatial bounds)** for every multiindex $\alpha\in\mathbb N^3$ with
  $|\alpha|\le2$ and every $\mathbf x\in K$,

$$|\partial^\alpha\varphi(\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{00}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|+|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^{|\alpha|}}.$$

  (Derivatives are with respect to $x^1,x^2,x^3$; here $|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}|$
  is the maximum over $i,j$ and $|\partial^\alpha r_{0i}|$ is the maximum
  over $i$.)

**(b) Derived data.** For stationary weak-field data define the
**spatial potential**

$$\Phi:=\varepsilon c^2\varphi\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a smooth spatial function of dimension $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ in the
framework's unit conventions; its pullback to $\Omega$ is stationary. The
symmetric component family $g(\varepsilon)-\eta$ is the **perturbation of the
family**.

**(c) Einstein families.** Stationary weak-field data form an **Einstein
family with coupling $\kappa$** when for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$
there is a smooth symmetric component field $T_{ab}(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ on
$\Omega$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) satisfying

$$G_{ab}\bigl(g(\varepsilon)\bigr)=\kappa\,T_{ab}(\varepsilon)\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection of
$g(\varepsilon)$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). In that case define the
**spatial density read from the time-time component**

$$\rho_\varepsilon(\mathbf x):=\frac{T_{00}(\varepsilon,x^0,\mathbf x)}{c^2}\qquad\text{on }U,$$

where any $x^0$ with $(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\Omega$ may be used. This is
well-defined: the metric is the pullback of spatial functions, so its
coordinate curvature components, and hence $T_{00}=\kappa^{-1}G_{00}$, are
constant on each fiber of $\pi$, including when that fiber is disconnected.
It has units $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; it is a coordinate-component
density and is not thereby the dust rest-mass density.

**(d) Scope.** This item fixes a class of metric families and the vocabulary
of the weak-field bridge: the spatial factorization, component form,
stationarity, spatial derivative bounds, potential, and the equation that
upgrades the data to an Einstein family. It asserts neither existence for prescribed data nor that $\partial_0$ is
timelike or a Killing field, that the inverse metrics are uniformly bounded,
or that $\rho_\varepsilon$ is positive; the latter properties are
consequences proved separately where they are used. The family is an explicit
input-family hypothesis: neither its existence for prescribed Newtonian
initial data nor its construction from other data is claimed. The physical
reading of the components, of $G_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$, of $\Phi$ and of
$\rho_\varepsilon$ belongs to the framework's postulates and unit
conventions, which are separate items.

This item fixes the unit and coordinate readings of the explicitly defined
Lorentzian objects, smooth-curve proper time and four-velocity of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and the constructed connection,
curvature, Ricci and scalar fields of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]].
It states conventions, not a physical law or a measurement.

**(a) Constants and tensor slot.** Adopt $c>0$ with SI dimension
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, $G_N>0$ with dimension
$\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{-2}$, and a signed parameter
$\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. No numerical value is asserted.
Define $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, of dimension
$\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^2$.
For a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $T$ adopt the convention that its
components $T_{AB}=T(e_A,e_B)$ in an ordered $g$-orthonormal basis are energy
per volume, $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.
This is a tensor slot and unit convention; interpreting a particular $T$ as
matter is a subsequent definition. Therefore $\kappa T_{AB}$ has dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$. No positivity, conservation or matter realization is assumed.

**(b) Coordinates and dimensions.** In a length-coordinate chart,
$x^0=ct$ and all four coordinates have units $\mathrm m$; $g_{ab}$ are
dimensionless and the quadratic line element $ds^2=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has units
$\mathrm m^2$. The Christoffel symbols defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) have units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$: the constructed formula differentiates dimensionless
$g_{ab}$ once with respect to a length coordinate. Curvature components have
units $\mathrm m^{-2}$ since the curvature operator differentiates the
connection once more and includes products of two connection coefficients;
so do $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and scalar curvature $S$ in these coordinates.
In a time-coordinate chart $x^0=t$ has units $\mathrm s$, and $g_{00}$ has
units $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$; mixed, spatial, angular or other chart
components have the dimensions obtained by the coordinate Jacobians. A single
component has no universal dimension in a general chart. Orthonormal-frame
readings use the normalized geometric basis, with its length normalization.

**(c) Curves and invariant readings.** For the smooth future timelike curve
and positive scaling parameter of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] (e),
read $c$ as in (a) and
$\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^{s}\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}\,dr$
as a proper-time parameter in seconds. Its four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$
has length-coordinate and normalized orthonormal components in
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$; in a time-coordinate chart $U^0=dt/d\tau$
is dimensionless and other component dimensions follow the coordinates.
Lorentzian length $c\,\Delta\tau$ is in metres. The tensors $R^g$,
$\operatorname{Ric}$ and the scalar $S$ have the orthonormal readings
$\mathrm m^{-2}$, whereas the lowered curvature components in a mixed chart
have the units required by the metric and coordinate slots.

**(d) Future observer readings and SI restoration.** Let $n$ be a future
unit timelike vector, $g(n,n)=-1$ and $g(n,N)<0$. Define
$\rho_n:=T(n,n)$, $j_n:=-\sharp(T(n,\cdot))$ and its spatial part
$\phi_n:=j_n-\rho_n n$; indeed $g(j_n,n)=-\rho_n$, so
$g(\phi_n,n)=0$. In a $g$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n$, set
$\phi^i=-T(e_0,e_i)=T^{0i}$ for $i=1,2,3$. The **SI energy flux** vector
and **SI momentum density** covector are, respectively,

$$q_n:=c\phi_n,\qquad p_n:=\phi_n^{\flat}/c,\qquad q_n^i=-cT_{0i},\qquad (p_n)_i=-T_{0i}/c.$$

Thus $\rho_n$ and each $\phi^i$ have units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$;
$q_n^i$ has units $\mathrm W\,\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $(p_n)_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$. Stress components $T_{ij}$ have
units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{Pa}$. Tensor components retain the
common energy-density units; the factors of $c$ convert their mixed readings
to different SI quantities. Future-directedness and the signs here are part
of the convention, not positivity assumptions on $T$.

**(e) Natural units.** Setting $c=1$, or additionally $G_N=1$, abbreviates
these dimensionful conventions. Restore the factors displayed above before
comparison with SI quantities; in particular the same spatial tensor component
corresponds to energy flux multiplied by $c$ and momentum density divided by
$c$. In a chart whose coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ are all lengths and whose
metric components are $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, a nonzero null tangent
vector $v=(v^0,\mathbf v)$, null as in clause (b) of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], satisfies
$\|\mathbf v\|_2:=\sqrt{(v^1)^2+(v^2)^2+(v^3)^2}=|v^0|$. Since $v\ne0$, this
implies $v^0\ne0$, so $\|\mathbf v\|_2/|v^0|=1$. This is a coordinate identity
for the null condition, not a postulate about light propagation, and it does
not change the physical constant $c$.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the matter-content
assumptions of the framework, the following rules by which ideal clocks, test
bodies and light couple to the metric $g$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].

**(i) Ideal clocks.** An **ideal clock** is an idealized physical device
carried along a future timelike worldline ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]])
whose readings are assumed to reproduce the proper time of that worldline:
the difference of two readings taken at two events of the worldline is the
proper-time increment between those events as defined by the metric, and it is
independent of the construction of the clock. Two ideal clocks moving along
the same worldline differ only by an additive constant (their choice of zero);
different worldlines generally accrue different proper times between the same
pair of events. The physical constant $c$ and the unit of duration are those
of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(ii) Free fall of massive test bodies.** A **test body** is an uncharged
idealized body whose internal structure is small compared with the scale over
which the geometry of the model varies and whose gravitational self-field is
negligible within the model. An **ideal freely falling massive test body** is
assumed to have a worldline that is a future timelike geodesic of the
metric-selected connection ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]), traversed with physical
four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$ satisfying
$g_{\gamma(\tau)}(U,U)=-c^2$; proper time is an affine parameter of the
worldline ([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). The
worldline is determined by the event at which the body is released together
with its four-velocity there, by the uniqueness of the geodesic initial-value
problem ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]); no force, charge, or
rest mass of the body enters this rule.

**(iii) Light rays.** In the geometric-optics approximation an **ideal light
ray** propagating in the model is assumed to be a future null geodesic of the
metric-selected connection
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]). A null worldline carries no proper
time and no four-velocity in the sense of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; within the approximation the
propagation of an ideal ray is independent of its frequency, and only the
ray's direction in the tangent space is fixed, not a scale along it.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** The three rules are adopted in the test-field
regime of the smooth classical model: the clocks, bodies and rays do not
back-react on the geometry, and the geometry varies smoothly on the scales
relevant to them. Configurations requiring the body's own gravitational field,
radiation reaction, an electromagnetic or other self-force, finite-size or
tidal couplings beyond the test-body idealization, non-geometric-optics
propagation, dispersion or dissipation of light, or quantum effects are
outside these assumptions and require additional model content. The
assumptions do not assert that any real clock, body or light ray is exactly
ideal, nor do they attach measured readings to any model.

Let a model of the classical gravitational framework be specified by a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ with its
metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and assume the
clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$U_0\in T_pM$ be a future timelike unit vector,
$g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

Suppose $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two ideal freely falling massive test bodies of
the model that are released at the event $p$ with physical four-velocity $U_0$:
their worldlines $\gamma_i:I_i\to M$ pass through $p$ and their four-vectors
there equal $U_0$. Let $\tau_i$ be their proper times, with origins chosen so
that $0\in I_i$ and $\gamma_i(0)=p$. Let
$\gamma_{p,U_0}:I_{p,U_0}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic through
$(p,U_0)$. Then each physical worldline is a restriction of that maximal
geodesic:

$$I_i\subseteq I_{p,U_0},\qquad \gamma_i(\tau)=\gamma_{p,U_0}(\tau)\quad(\tau\in I_i),\qquad i=1,2.$$

In particular, $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ coincide wherever both are defined.
The theorem does not assume that either physical worldline has the entire
maximal geodesic's domain. The unique geodesic continuation is determined by
the release event and the initial four-velocity alone; parameters that
distinguish the two bodies, such as their rest masses, do not enter.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the velocity derivation of
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] translated to the parameter
value $t$. In a chart around $\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** A **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.


**(d) Intrinsic construction before physical use.** For smooth local vector
fields define the Koszul expression

$$K(X,Y,Z):=Xg(Y,Z)+Yg(Z,X)-Zg(X,Y)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X).$$

Define $\nabla^g_XY$ by $2g(\nabla^g_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)$ for every smooth local
$Z$. The proof below establishes existence, smoothness, the affine-connection
rules, metric compatibility, torsion freedom and uniqueness; it uses symmetry
and nondegeneracy, not positive definiteness. Thus $\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$
has this unique element, called the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$. The later
nondegenerate-metric theorem retains its fuller tensor-derivative statement.
Its Christoffel symbols in any chart are defined by
$\nabla^g_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]) and obey

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12 g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}),\qquad a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3.$$

**(e) Basic curvature and contractions.** The **curvature** of this connection
is the operator of [[def-curvature-of-an-affine-connection]], with the fixed
sign convention

$$R^g(X,Y)Z:=\nabla^g_X\nabla^g_YZ-\nabla^g_Y\nabla^g_XZ-\nabla^g_{[X,Y]}Z.$$

The general affine-connection theorem
[[thm-curvature-is-a-type-one-three-tensor]] proves that it depends pointwise
only on $X,Y,Z$ and is a smooth tensor. Define its chart components by
$R^g(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$.
Define the **Ricci tensor** and **scalar curvature** pointwise by

$$\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,w):=\operatorname{tr}(z\mapsto R^g_p(z,w)v),\qquad S(p):=\operatorname{tr}(\sharp_p\circ\operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p),\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{\flat}_p(v):=\operatorname{Ric}_p(v,\cdot).$$

Here $\sharp$ is the inverse metric isomorphism and traces are the
basis-independent trace of [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. Equivalently,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=\sum_aR^a{}_{bad}$ and
$S=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}$, all sums from $0$ through $3$.
These are well-defined smooth fields by finite contraction of the smooth
components of $R^g$ and $g^{-1}$; basis independence follows from the trace
and the intrinsic maps just defined. No symmetry identity or field equation
is assumed here. Lowering the curvature output gives
$R_{abcd}=g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd}$, so the definitions agree with the full later
curvature item, which proves the remaining symmetries and coordinate formulas.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$ and compact $K\subseteq U$, and suppose the
data form an Einstein family with coupling $\kappa>0$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]] clauses (a)-(c)). Write
$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$,
$\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2:U\to\mathbb R$, and let $G^{(1)}$ be the
first-order Einstein coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N:=\kappa c^4/(8\pi)$. There are $\varepsilon_*'>0$, depending only on $\varepsilon_0$, $C$,
$L$ and the dimension, and $C_2<\infty$, depending only on $C$, $L$ and
the dimension, such that for every
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*'$ the following inequalities hold at every
spacetime point $p\in\Omega$ with $\pi(p)\in K$. Spatial derivatives and
$\Delta$ are taken on $U$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), and maxima
are over the free component indices.

**(a) Linearized approximation.** With
$A_{ab}(\varepsilon):=g_{ab}(\varepsilon)-\eta_{ab}$,

$$\bigl|G_{ab}(g(\varepsilon))-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A(\varepsilon))\bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2} .$$

**(b) Component hierarchy of the Einstein tensor.**

$$\Bigl|G_{00}(g(\varepsilon))-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{ij}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{0i}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

**(c) Stress hierarchy and independent dust source.** The Einstein equation
gives

$$\Bigl|\kappa T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{ij}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{0i}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

For every Einstein family, the definition $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$ therefore gives
$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\rho_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{2L^2}.$$

For the additional conclusion below, let $\nabla^\varepsilon$ denote the
metric-selected connection of $g(\varepsilon)$ and assume the Einstein source is an
**independent admissible nonnegative dust input**: for each $\varepsilon$,
there are smooth fields $\mathcal E_\varepsilon:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ and
$u_\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, with $u_\varepsilon$ future-directed and
$g(\varepsilon)(u_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)=-1$, such that
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon (u_\varepsilon)_a(u_\varepsilon)_b$ and
$$\nabla^\varepsilon_a(\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_\varepsilon^a)=0,\qquad u_\varepsilon^a\nabla^\varepsilon_a u_\varepsilon^b=0 .$$
Where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon>0$, this is the dust model of
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; where it vanishes, the smooth field
$u_\varepsilon$ remains specified and satisfies the geodesic equation by
the explicit hypotheses above. The stress
conservation identity follows from these equations (and agrees on the
positive-density region with [[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]).
No comoving condition is imposed: the spatial tilt may be nonzero.
Define the independent rest-mass density
$$\mu_\varepsilon:=\mathcal E_\varepsilon/c^2\quad[\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}],$$
where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ has the rest-energy-density unit
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mu_\varepsilon$ is independent of the
coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon$.
It factors through $\pi$: normalization gives $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=-g^{ab}T_{ab}=-\kappa^{-1}g^{ab}G_{ab}$, whose components factor through the spatial projection by the Einstein-family hypothesis. Thus $\mu_\varepsilon$ also denotes its resulting smooth spatial function on $U$, including on disconnected fibers.
On $K$, assume the explicit weak-source and tilted slow-motion bounds
$$0\le\mathcal E_\varepsilon\le\frac{C\varepsilon c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad s_\varepsilon\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\,c,$$
where on the region over $K$ the time orientation is chosen so that
$\partial_0$ is future (and $g(u_\varepsilon,\partial_0)<0$), and
$n_\varepsilon:=\partial_0/\sqrt{-g_{00}}$ is the resulting future unit
coordinate observer, $\gamma_\varepsilon:=-g(u_\varepsilon,n_\varepsilon)$,
$h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon):=u_\varepsilon+g(n_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)n_\varepsilon$,
and $s_\varepsilon$ is the norm of
$c\,h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)/\gamma_\varepsilon$ in the observer's
rest space ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
[[lem-gr-observer-relative-velocity-expansions]]). Choose
$$\varepsilon_*'\le\min\{\varepsilon_0,1,(128C)^{-1},(4C^2)^{-1}\},$$
also small enough for the two-jet estimate in the proof. This threshold
condition is dimensionless.
Then, for a constant $C_d$ depending only on $C$,

$$|T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\mu_\varepsilon c^2|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad |\rho_\varepsilon-\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^2}{G_NL^2},$$

and the distinct dust rest-mass density satisfies the Poisson estimate

$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{L^2} .$$

The energy- and mass-density conventions of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
give the same tensor here:
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_a u_b=c^2\mu_\varepsilon u_a u_b$,
with $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=c^2\mu_\varepsilon$.

**(d) Scaled dust source.** Let $X:=\mathbf x/L$ and
$U_L:=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$. Define
$\psi(X):=\varphi(LX)$ and
$R(X):=G_NL^2\mu_\varepsilon(LX)/(\varepsilon c^2)$ on $U_L$, with
$\Delta_X$ the Laplacian in $X$. Then

$$|\Delta_X\psi-4\pi R|\le C_2\varepsilon\qquad\text{on }K/L .$$

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$U\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open subset, the **matter domain**, carrying its
restricted smooth structure
([[prop-an-open-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold-has-a-canonical-restricted-smooth-structure]]).

**(a) Data.** A **dust model** on $U$ is a pair $(\rho,u)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\rho:U\to\mathbb R$ with $\rho(p)>0$ for every $p\in U$,
  the **rest density**; and
- a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ on $U$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]] with target $TM$
  described through the tangent bundle; concretely, $u$ is a smooth vector
  field on $U$ with $g_p(u_p,u_p)=-1$ and $g_p(u_p,N_p)<0$ at every $p$,
  [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

The parameter $\rho$ is the coefficient in the unit-normalized tensor of
clause (b); this mathematical definition assigns it no physical unit. In the
framework's SI stress-energy reading it is the **rest energy density**
$\varepsilon:=\rho$, in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$. The **rest-mass
density** is instead $\rho_m:=\varepsilon/c^2$, in
$\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the physical four-velocity is
$U:=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Thus the same tensor is
$T^{ab}=\varepsilon u^au^b=\rho_m U^aU^b$. A purely mathematical or
$c=1$ convention may rescale the density coefficient; interpreting $\rho$
as an SI mass density while keeping the unit tangent $u$ would require the
explicit tensor $c^2\rho\,u\otimes u$. Physical realizations and readings
are adopted by the matter postulate, not deduced here.

**(b) Stress-energy tensor.** The model's **stress-energy tensor** is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T^{ab}:=\rho\,u^au^b\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T_{ab}=\rho\,u_au_b,$$

with $u_a=g_{ac}u^c$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]); the two expressions correspond
under raising both indices, by $g^{ac}g^{bd}T_{cd}=T^{ab}$.

**(c) Dust system.** The **dust system** on $U$ is the pair of equations

$$\nabla_a(\rho\,u^a)=0,\qquad u^a\nabla_au^b=0 .$$

The first is a continuity equation for the density current $\rho u$; the
second says that the integral curves of $u$ are geodesics in the parameter that
makes $u$ their unit tangent, i.e. that the dust particles are in free fall
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Newtonian comparison model.** A **Newtonian comparison model** is a

- a $C^\infty$ function $\Phi_N:O\to\mathbb R$, the **Newtonian potential**,
  whose values are read in $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$;
- a $C^\infty$ function $\rho_N:O\to\mathbb R$, the **Newtonian mass
  density**, whose values are read in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; and
- a real constant $G_{\mathrm{cmp}}>0$ with the dimension
  $\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$,

such that the **Newtonian field equation**

$$\Delta\Phi_N=4\pi G_{\mathrm{cmp}}\rho_N\qquad\text{on }O$$

([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). A **comparison motion** of the model is

$$q''(t)=-\nabla\Phi_N\bigl(q(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$

where in the standard coordinates of $\mathbb R^3$
$\nabla\Phi_N(q):=(\partial_1\Phi_N(q),\partial_2\Phi_N(q),\partial_3\Phi_N(q))$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) and the total derivative is the
covector represented by this vector through the Euclidean inner product:
$D\Phi_N(q)[v]=\langle\nabla\Phi_N(q),v\rangle$
([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]],
[[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

of the definition of the comparison framework and are not derived here from

$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$ and $c>0$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]), let $\varepsilon_*$ and $C_2$ be
the threshold and constant of
[[lem-gr-weak-field-christoffel-bounds]], let $S_*>0$ and
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$, and put
$T_\varepsilon:=LS_*/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$,
$U_L:=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$, and
$\psi(X):=\varphi(LX)$ for $X\in U_L$.

$\langle X,Y\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^3X^iY^i$ and norm
$\|X\|_2=\sqrt{\langle X,X\rangle}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). In the standard coordinates,
$\nabla\psi=(\partial_{X^1}\psi,\partial_{X^2}\psi,\partial_{X^3}\psi)$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]); write

  $X_*([0,S_*])\subseteq K'$ and

$\sup_{0\le S\le S_*}D(S)\le C_3\varepsilon S_*e^{(1+K_2)S_*}=O(\varepsilon)$.

$T_\varepsilon=LS_*/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$, so the fixed scaled interval
$[0,S_*]$ corresponds to coordinate times growing like
$\varepsilon^{-1/2}$; the limit statement is therefore not a large-$t$
statement at fixed $\varepsilon$.

derivations.claim: (Field and source correspondence.) By [A1] and [A3], the given Einstein family and its independently specified dust input satisfy the restricted field-law and dust hypotheses of [[thm-gr-weak-field-einstein-stress-hierarchy]]. Apply [L1]. Its first stress estimate gives the displayed component hierarchy, and its dust conclusion gives the error between $\Delta\Phi$ and $4\pi G_N\mu_\varepsilon$. By [L2], $\Delta\Phi_N=4\pi G_N\rho_N$ and $\Phi_N=\Phi$ exactly, so subtraction and division by $4\pi G_N>0$ yield $|\rho_N-\mu_\varepsilon|\le C_2\varepsilon^2c^2/(4\pi G_NL^2)$. The coordinate density satisfies the separate estimate in [L1]; neither density identification is exact. This proves (a).

(Free fall to the acceleration bound.) By [A2], the assigned worldline is the model's future timelike geodesic with the stated proper-time and initial data conditions. Its spatial path lies in $K$, has coordinate time $t=x^0/c$ and meets the speed bound in the Statement. The mathematical coordinate-time acceleration estimate [[lem-gr-weak-field-geodesic-acceleration]] therefore applies and gives clause (b).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). The cotangent space $T_p^*M$ is
the algebraic dual of $T_pM$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**Musical isomorphisms.** Define the **flat map**

$$\flat_p:T_pM\longrightarrow T_p^*M,\qquad \flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot),$$

so that $\flat_p(v)(w)=g_p(v,w)$; it is $\mathbb R$-linear by bilinearity of
$g_p$. Its kernel is $\{v:g_p(v,w)=0\text{ for all }w\}=\{0\}$ because $g_p$ is
nondegenerate, and $\dim_{\mathbb R}T_pM=\dim_{\mathbb R}T_p^*M=4$ since the
coordinate derivations of a chart form a basis of $T_pM$
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]); hence
$\flat_p$ is a linear isomorphism and has an inverse
$\sharp_p:T_p^*M\to T_pM$.

**Inverse metric.** The **inverse metric** at $p$ is the symmetric bilinear form

$$g_p^{-1}:T_p^*M\times T_p^*M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta).$$

It is symmetric because $g_p$ is, and it is nondegenerate: if
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta)=0$ for all $\beta$, then $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\cdot)=0$,
so $\sharp_p\alpha=0$ and hence $\alpha=0$.

**Components in a chart.** Let $(U,x)$ be a smooth chart and
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ the components of $g$; let
$dx^a|_q$ be the differential of the coordinate function $x^a$ at $q$
([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]), so that
$dx^a|_q(\partial_b|_q)=\partial_b|_q(x^a)=\delta^a{}_b$. Define the components
of the inverse metric in this chart by

$$g^{ab}(q):=g_q^{-1}\bigl(dx^a|_q,\,dx^b|_q\bigr),\qquad q\in U,$$

so that $\sharp_q(dx^a|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)\,\partial_b|_q$; equivalently
$(g^{ab}(q))$ is the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab}(q))$ at every $q$, that is

$$g^{ac}(q)\,g_{cb}(q)=\delta^a{}_b,\qquad g_{ac}(q)g^{cb}(q)=\delta_a{}^b,$$

because $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=dx^a|_q(\partial_c|_q)=\delta^a{}_c$
and also $g_q(\sharp_qdx^a|_q,\partial_c|_q)=\sum_bg^{ab}(q)g_{bc}(q)$. In
particular $g^{ab}=g^{ba}$. The components $g^{ab}$ depend smoothly on $q$;
this is proved in [[lem-gr-inverse-metric-is-smooth]].

**Raising, lowering and metric trace.** Let $A$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on an open set $V\subseteq M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). At each $p\in V$ define the
endomorphism

$$A^\sharp_p:T_pM\to T_pM,\qquad A^\sharp_p(v):=\sharp_p\bigl(A_p(v,\cdot)\bigr),$$

characterized by $g_p(A^\sharp_p(v),w)=A_p(v,w)$ for all $w\in T_pM$; it is
self-adjoint for $g_p$ because $A_p$ is symmetric. Its **metric trace** is

$$\operatorname{tr}_g(A)(p):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A^\sharp_p\bigr)$$

with the trace of an endomorphism as in [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. In a
chart the raised, mixed and doubly raised components are

$$A^{ab}:=g^{ac}g^{bd}A_{cd},\qquad A^a{}_b:=g^{ac}A_{cb},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{tr}_g(A)=g^{ab}A_{ab},$$

the last identity obtained by evaluating in a $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, where $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$ by
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] so that
$g^{ab}A_{ab}=\sum_a g^{aa}A_{aa}=-A(e_0,e_0)+A(e_1,e_1)+A(e_2,e_2)+A(e_3,e_3)$,
which is the trace of the endomorphism $v\mapsto\sharp_p(A_p(v,\cdot))$ in that
basis. All these operations are pointwise and depend only on $g$, $A$ and the
duality pairing, not on a chart.

**Conventions.** Raising and lowering apply to one index at a time and preserve
index order; $A_{ab}$, $A^a{}_b$ and $A^{ab}$ denote the same tensor $A$ with
indices positioned by $g$. The musical isomorphisms and the inverse metric are
defined for every smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of this library; no choice
principle is used in this definition, every ingredient being pointwise linear
algebra over $\mathbb R$ together with the pointwise nondegeneracy of $g_p$.

first-order coefficients $\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$, $S^{(1)}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}$ and with trace
reversal $\bar h$, d'Alembertian $\Box$ and gauge transformation
$h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ as in
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], and let $L>0$ be a length scale.
All components are taken in the inertial chart and all contractions are
with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$.

**(a) Christoffel symbols.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there is a
constant $C_K<\infty$ such that for all $p\in K$ and
$0<|\lambda|\le\varepsilon_1/2$,

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,\eta^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bh_{cd}+\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(b) Ricci tensor.** With the same constants (enlarged if necessary),

$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** In this clause, suprema of the nonnegative
component magnitudes over an empty set are defined to be $0$. For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Then $\nabla f$ is a $C^1$ field on $U$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], since each of its components $\partial_if$ has continuous first partial derivatives, so its divergence is defined; the **Laplacian** of $f$ is

$$\Delta f:=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_{i<n}\partial_i\partial_if,$$

with the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. A $C^2$ function with $\Delta f=0$ on $U$ is called **harmonic** on $U$.

For a $C^2$ map $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{q-1}):U\to\mathbb R^q$, whose components are $C^2$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], $\Delta F$ is the field whose $i$th coordinate is $\Delta F_i$. In the three-coordinate naming of this page, $\Delta f=\partial_x\partial_xf+\partial_y\partial_yf+\partial_z\partial_zf$ and $\Delta F=(\Delta F_x,\Delta F_y,\Delta F_z)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), so that at every $p\in M$ the form
$g_p$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$, and let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field on $M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) whose
support is compact.

**(a) Pointwise openness.** Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $4$
and let $G$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$ of inertia $(3,1,0)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). If in some basis of $V$ the matrix of $G$
has the form $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E$, then $G$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$
whenever $|E_{ij}|<1/8$ for all $i,j$. Consequently, for every basis the set
of matrices of symmetric forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$ is open in the space
$M_4^{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathbb R)$ with respect to the maximum-entry norm, and
equivalently $g_p$ has a neighborhood in the space of symmetric forms at $p$
consisting entirely of forms of inertia $(3,1,0)$.

**(b) Global stability.** There is $\lambda_0>0$ such that for every real
$\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<\lambda_0$ the smooth symmetric field $g+\lambda h$
is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $M$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with
time orientation inherited from $N$ (the field $N$ remains timelike for
$g+\lambda h$ for $|\lambda|$ small).

derivations.claim: (Admissibility.) In the coordinate frame the components of $\lambda h$ are $\lambda h_{00}=-2\lambda\varphi$, $\lambda h_{ij}=-2\lambda\varphi\delta_{ij}$ and $0$ otherwise, so the matrix of $g(\lambda)=\eta+\lambda h$ in the coordinate basis is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)+E(\lambda)$ with $E(\lambda)=-2\lambda\varphi\,I_4$, the entries of which satisfy $|E(\lambda)_{ij}|=2|\lambda|\,\varphi<2\cdot\tfrac18\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac18$ on $\Omega$, because $\varphi<\tfrac12$ there; all components are stationary and smooth, so $g(\lambda)$ is a smooth symmetric component field. By [L5] $g(\lambda)$ has inertia $(3,1,0)$ for every $0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$, and $q\equiv0$ is smooth; hence $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ satisfies clause (a) of [L1].

(First-order connection.) By [L2] and [L3], $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{00}=\tfrac12\eta^{ia}(2\partial_0h_{a0}-\partial_ah_{00})$. The time derivatives vanish and $\partial_ah_{00}=-2\partial_a\varphi$, so $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{00}=\eta^{ia}\partial_a\varphi=\partial^i\varphi=x^i$. Similarly $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{0j}=\tfrac12\eta^{ia}(\partial_0h_{aj}+\partial_jh_{a0}-\partial_ah_{0j})=0$ and $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{j0}=0$ because the spatial components $h_{k0}=h_{0k}$ vanish and $\eta^{i0}=0$. For the spatial pairs $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{jk}=\tfrac12\eta^{ia}(\partial_jh_{ak}+\partial_kh_{aj}-\partial_ah_{jk}) =\tfrac12\delta^{ia}\bigl(-2\partial_j\varphi\,\delta_{ak}-2\partial_k\varphi\,\delta_{aj}+2\partial_a\varphi\,\delta_{jk}\bigr) =-\delta^i_kx_j-\delta^i_jx_k+\delta_{jk}x^i$. For the components with upper index $0$, $\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\eta^{0a}(\partial_bh_{ca}+\partial_ch_{ba}-\partial_ah_{bc}) =-\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_bh_{c0}+\partial_ch_{b0}-\partial_0h_{bc}\bigr)$, since $\eta^{0a}$ is nonzero only at $a=0$: for $(b,c)=(0,0)$ and for $b,c$ both spatial this vanishes ($h_{i0}=0$ for spatial $i$ and all component time derivatives vanish), while $\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{0i}=\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{i0}=-\tfrac12\partial_ih_{00}=\partial_i\varphi=x_i$.

(Trace data.) By [L2], $h=\eta^{ab}h_{ab}=\eta^{00}h_{00}+\eta^{ij}h_{ij}=2\varphi-6\varphi=-4\varphi$, and the mixed components $h^{c}{}_{b}=\eta^{ca}h_{ab}$ are $h^{0}{}_{0}=\eta^{00}h_{00}=2\varphi$, $h^{i}{}_{j}=\eta^{ik}h_{kj}=-2\varphi\delta^i_j$, $h^{0}{}_{i}=\eta^{0a}h_{ai}=0$ and $h^{i}{}_{0}=\eta^{ik}h_{k0}=0$.

(First-order Ricci tensor.) By [L3] and step 1.3: for the $(00)$ component, $\partial_c\partial_0h^{c}{}_{0}=0$ because all components of $h^{c}{}_{0}$ are stationary, and $-\Box h_{00}-\partial_0\partial_0h=2\Box\varphi=2\Delta\varphi=6$ (the field $h$ is stationary), so $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{00}=\tfrac12(0+0+6+0)=3$. For the $(0i)$ component, $\partial_c\partial_0h^{c}{}_{i}=0$ and $\partial_c\partial_ih^{c}{}_{0}=0$ because the fields $h^{c}{}_{i}$ are stationary and $h^{c}{}_{0}$ vanishes for $c\ne0$ and is stationary for $c=0$; and $\Box h_{0i}=\partial_0\partial_ih=0$ because $h_{0i}=0$ and $h$ is stationary; so $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{0i}=0$. For the $(ij)$ component, $\partial_c\partial_ih^{c}{}_{j}=\partial_k\partial_i(-2\varphi\delta^k_j)=-2\delta_{ij}$, likewise $\partial_c\partial_jh^{c}{}_{i}=-2\delta_{ij}$, $-\Box h_{ij}=2\delta_{ij}\Delta\varphi=6\delta_{ij}$ and $-\partial_i\partial_jh=4\partial_i\partial_j\varphi=4\delta_{ij}$, so $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ij}=\tfrac12(-2-2+6+4)\delta_{ij}=3\delta_{ij}$.

(Scalar curvature.) By [L3] and [L2], $\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}=\partial_i\partial_jh^{ij}=\partial_i\partial_j(-2\varphi\delta^{ij})=-2\Delta\varphi=-6$, since $h^{00}=-2\varphi$, $h^{0i}=0$, $h^{ij}=-2\varphi\delta^{ij}$ and all time derivatives vanish; and $\Box h=\Box(-4\varphi)=-4\Delta\varphi=-12$. Hence $S^{(1)}=-6+12=6$. As an arithmetic check on the defining relation $S=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], whose first-order expansion at $\lambda=0$ is $S^{(1)}=\eta^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$ because $\operatorname{Ric}(0)=0$: the values of step 2.1 give $-\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{00}+\delta^{ij}\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ij}=-3+9=6$, in agreement.

(Einstein tensor and cross-check.) By [L2] the trace reversal of step 1.3 is $\bar h_{00}=h_{00}-\tfrac12\eta_{00}h=-2\varphi-\tfrac12(-1)(-4\varphi)=-4\varphi$, $\bar h_{ij}=-2\varphi\delta_{ij}-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}(-4\varphi)=0$ and $\bar h_{0i}=0$; that is, $\bar h_{ab}=-4\varphi\,\delta_{a0}\delta_{b0}$. The closed formula of [L3] then gives: for $(00)$, $\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}=\eta^{00}\eta^{00}\partial_0\partial_0\bar h_{00}=0$ and $\partial^c\partial_{(0}\bar h_{0)c}=0$ by stationarity, so $G^{(1)}_{00}=-\tfrac12\Box(-4\varphi)=2\Delta\varphi=6$; for $(0i)$ and $(ij)$ every term of the closed formula involves a component $\bar h_{0\cdot}$ or a time derivative, hence vanishes, so $G^{(1)}_{0i}=G^{(1)}_{ij}=0$. Finally, the values satisfy $G^{(1)}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}-\tfrac12\eta_{ab}S^{(1)}$: $3-\tfrac12(-1)(6)=6$ for $(00)$, $3\delta_{ij}-\tfrac12\delta_{ij}\cdot6=0$ for $(ij)$ and $0-0=0$ for $(0i)$, which is the first-order expansion at $\lambda=0$ of the defining relation $G=\operatorname{Ric}-\tfrac12Sg$ of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]], using $S(0)=0$ and $g(0)=\eta$.
