citations.quote:
Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ carry its standard smooth structure
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and let
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ be the **identity chart**, $x(p)=p$;
it is a global chart of the maximal smooth atlas, and the coordinate
derivations $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ form a basis of
$T_pM$ at every $p\in M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). Write

$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$$

for the standard Lorentz form of inertia $(3,1,0)$ in this basis
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

**(a) The metric.** Define the covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$ by the
requirement that its components in the identity chart are the constants

$$g_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}\qquad(a,b=0,1,2,3),$$

that is, $g_p(\partial_a|_p,\partial_b|_p)=\eta_{ab}$ for every $p\in M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] clause (a)). The component
functions are constant, hence $C^\infty$, so $g$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field; at every $p$ the form $g_p$ is nondegenerate with
inertia $(3,1,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a) the
pair $(M,g)$ is therefore a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$.

**(b) The inertial chart and frame.** The chart $x$ is called the **inertial
chart** of the flat model. In this chart the coordinate frame
$(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is a $g$-orthonormal frame at
every point, $g(\partial_a,\partial_b)=\eta_{ab}$; it is simultaneously a
coordinate frame and a **tetrad field** in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], defined on all of $M$.

**(c) Time orientation and causal classification.** Define the smooth vector
field $N:=\partial_0$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)=\eta_{00}=-1<0$ for every $p$, the field $N$ is everywhere
timelike, so $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). For a nonzero tangent
vector $v=v^a\partial_a|_p$ the definitions of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c) and
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] give

$$g_p(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2,\qquad g_p(v,N_p)=-v^0 .$$

so $v$ is **future-directed** exactly when $v^0>0$, and

- $v$ is future timelike $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2>\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is future null $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2=\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is spacelike $\iff$ $(v^0)^2<\sum_i(v^i)^2$;

consequently the future causal cone at every point is
$\{v\neq0: v^0\ge\sqrt{\sum_i(v^i)^2}\}$. These are the standard readings of
the Minkowski form in the inertial chart; the chain of equivalences is the
specialization of the causal classification to this pair $(g_p,N_p)$ and is
recorded here for later use.

**(d) Scope.** This item defines geometric data only: a manifold, a metric
field, a time orientation and a distinguished chart and frame. It makes no
claim about curvature, about any field equation, about which geometry a
physical model uses, or about nature; the physical reading of the data, the
dimensions of the coordinates and the numerical values or signs of physical
constants belong to the framework's unit conventions and postulates, which
are separate items. In particular no relation between the coordinate
functions $x^a$ and physical time or length measurements is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with its inertial chart $x$,
and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Vanishing connection.** In the inertial chart all Christoffel symbols
of $\nabla$ vanish identically:

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\equiv0\qquad(a,b,c=0,1,2,3).$$

**(b) Vanishing curvature.** The curvature operator of $\nabla$ vanishes
identically, $R\equiv0$; consequently the curvature components, the Ricci
tensor, the scalar curvature and the Einstein tensor vanish identically,

$$R^a{}_{bcd}\equiv0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\equiv0,\qquad S\equiv0,\qquad G_{ab}\equiv0 .$$

**(c) Translation Killing fields.** Each coordinate field $\partial_a$ is a
Killing field of $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]]); in particular the time
orientation field $N=\partial_0$ is a unit timelike Killing field.

**(d) Straight geodesics.** A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ on an interval
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) is a geodesic of $\nabla$ if and
only if there are $x_0,v\in\mathbb R^4$ such that

$$x\bigl(\gamma(s)\bigr)=x_0+s\,v\qquad(s\in I).$$

For such a geodesic the speed is constant,
$g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2$; the maximal
geodesic with $x(\gamma(0))=x_0$ and $x(\gamma)'(0)=v$ has domain
$\mathbb R$. If $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $v^0>0$, the geodesic is a future timelike
worldline
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) and, for any $s_0\in I$,
the parameter
$\tau(s):=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}\,(s-s_0)/c$ is proper time up to an additive
constant, with $d\gamma/d\tau$ the physical four-velocity
$U$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$
([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]] clause 3).

**(e) Inertial-chart velocity reading.** Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic as in
(d) with $x(\gamma(s))=x_0+sv$, $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $v^0>0$. Define
$t(s):=x^0(\gamma(s))/c=(x_0^0+sv^0)/c$; this is strictly increasing, and
on $t(I)$ define
$\gamma_t(t):=\gamma((ct-x_0^0)/v^0)$. Then
$x(\gamma_t(t))=(ct,\mathbf q(t))$ for its spatial component $\mathbf q$,
and the coordinate velocity is the constant vector
$\mathbf w:=d\mathbf q/dt=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$. With
$|\mathbf w|:=\|\mathbf w\|_2$ from the Euclidean inner product
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), timelikeness gives $|\mathbf w|<c$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the coordinate representative and its derivatives through order $k$
  are continuous up to $t_0$ on the relative interval
  $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$, with derivatives at
  $t_0$ taken one-sided. For $k=\infty$ this holds at every finite order.
  Merely possessing a one-sided secant tangent, as defined next, does not
  by itself make a curve $C^1$ at the endpoint. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $[s_{i-1},s_i]$ is $C^1$ up to its included
  endpoints in the one-sided sense above: in every endpoint chart its
  component derivatives on the open piece have continuous one-sided limits,
  agreeing with its endpoint derivatives. Equivalently each piece has a
  $C^1$ extension to its closed parameter piece. In particular its right
  tangent at $s_{i-1}$ and left tangent at $s_i$ exist. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. The piece extensions give continuity at the
  corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the velocity derivation of
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] translated to the parameter
value $t$. In a chart around $\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** A **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The continuous one-sided limits of the component derivatives, required
by the $C^1$ extension of each piece, and continuity of $g$ imply that
$h_i$ tends to the norm of the corresponding endpoint tangent. The future
timelike hypothesis on those tangents makes these limits strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
the function with $\tau(s_0)=0$ and $\tau(s)$ equal to the increment
from $s_0$ to $s$ when $s>s_0$, and minus the increment from $s$ to $s_0$
when $s<s_0$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$c>0$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

1. **Well-definedness and additivity of proper time.** Let
   $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike worldline
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then the sum defining
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)$ is the same for every admissible partition of $[a,b]$; it
   is written $\frac1c\int_a^b h$, where $h$ is the piecewise-defined
   proper-time density. For $a<c<b$,
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=\bigl(\tau(c)-\tau(a)\bigr)+\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(c)\bigr)$.
   If $a<b$, the increment is strictly positive.

2. **Reparametrization and orientation, including subintervals.** Let
   $a'<b'$ and let $\varphi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ be $C^1$ up to its included
   endpoints with nonzero derivative everywhere, including one-sided endpoint
   derivatives. Let $\tilde\gamma:=\gamma\circ\varphi$. Its derivative has
   constant sign and $\varphi$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism onto its actual image
   interval. If $\varphi'>0$, then $\tilde\gamma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ future
   timelike worldline and
   $$\tilde\tau(b')-\tilde\tau(a')=\tau(\varphi(b'))-\tau(\varphi(a')).$$
   This equals $\tau(b)-\tau(a)$ when $\varphi(a')=a$ and $\varphi(b')=b$.
   If $\varphi'<0$, then $\tilde\gamma$ is a piecewise-$C^1$ **past** timelike
   traversal. Its unsigned density
   $\tilde h=\sqrt{-g(\tilde\gamma',\tilde\gamma')}$ obeys
   $$\frac1c\int_{a'}^{b'}\tilde h=\tau(\varphi(a'))-\tau(\varphi(b'))>0,$$
   whereas the oriented original difference
   $\tau(\varphi(b'))-\tau(\varphi(a'))$ is negative. For endpoint-reversing
   $\varphi(a')=b$, $\varphi(b')=a$, the latter equals
   $-\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(a)\bigr)$. This negative oriented difference is not
   elapsed proper time for a future curve; parameter reversal reverses the
   causal direction. Non-surjective maps compare increments over their
   actual image interval, not over the whole original interval.

3. **Proper-time function and four-velocity.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a
   $C^1$ future timelike worldline on an interval with nonempty interior and
   let $\tau$ be its proper-time function based at $t_0\in I$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then $\tau$ is $C^1$ on
   $I$ with
   $$\tau'(t)=\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}>0,$$
   so $\tau$ is strictly increasing, and at every $t\in I$ the velocity,
   proper-time density and four-velocity satisfy
   $\gamma'(t)=\tau'(t)\,U(t)$ and $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$. If
   $\tau$ is strictly increasing on $I$ with image $J$, then the
   reparametrized curve $\gamma_\tau:=\gamma\circ(\tau|_I)^{-1}$ is a $C^1$
   future timelike worldline on $J$ with
   $$\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)=U\bigl(\tau^{-1}(\sigma)\bigr),\qquad g\bigl(\gamma_\tau'(\sigma),\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)\bigr)=-c^2 .$$
   The same formulas hold piece by piece for a piecewise-$C^1$ future
   timelike worldline, on each open piece and at its endpoints one-sided, with the two
   corner velocities kept distinct.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]], [[def-ordered-field]]) with its order
([[def-real-order]]).

A subset $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is **order-convex** when

$$x, y \in I \text{ and } x \le z \le y \;\Longrightarrow\; z \in I .$$

The **intervals** of $\mathbb{R}$ are the sets of the following nine forms, where
$a, b \in \mathbb{R}$:

| | bounded forms | | one-sided and full forms |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(a,b)$ | $\{x : a < x < b\}$ | $(a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a < x\}$ |
| $[a,b]$ | $\{x : a \le x \le b\}$ | $[a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a \le x\}$ |
| $[a,b)$ | $\{x : a \le x < b\}$ | $(-\infty,b)$ | $\{x : x < b\}$ |
| $(a,b]$ | $\{x : a < x \le b\}$ | $(-\infty,b]$ | $\{x : x \le b\}$ |
| | | $(-\infty,\infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ |

An interval is **open** when both of its written endpoints are excluded, that is
for the forms $(a,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b)$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$; it is
**closed** when both written endpoints are included, that is for $[a,b]$,
$[a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b]$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$. The forms $[a,b)$ and
$(a,b]$ are **half-open**.

**The symbols $\pm\infty$ are notation and not elements of $\mathbb{R}$.** They
mark which side carries no endpoint condition at all; the five forms in the right
column are defined by the displayed conditions on $x$ alone, and no arithmetic is
ever performed with $\infty$. This is the same refusal to extend $\mathbb{R}$
silently that [[rem-sup-conventions]] records for suprema.

**Every one of the nine forms is order-convex.** Each is defined by a conjunction
of at most two conditions, each of the shape $a < x$, $a \le x$, $x < b$ or
$x \le b$, and each such condition is inherited by an intermediate point: if
$a < x$ and $x \le z$ then $a < z$, and if $z \le y$ and $y < b$ then $z < b$,
by transitivity of the order ([[def-ordered-field]]). Applying this to whichever
one or two conditions define the form in question gives $z \in I$ whenever
$x, y \in I$ and $x \le z \le y$.

**Bounded intervals.** An interval is **bounded** ([[def-bounded-set]]) exactly
when it is of one of the four forms in the left column: for those, $a$ is a lower
bound and $b$ an upper bound. The other five forms are unbounded, on the side or
sides written with $\infty$; the verification is in the remarks below.

**Nondegeneracy.** An interval is **degenerate** when it has at most one element,
and **nondegenerate** when it has at least two. For the four bounded forms with
endpoints $a$ and $b$:

- $[a,b]$ is nonempty exactly when $a \le b$, and it is nondegenerate exactly
  when $a < b$. It is the singleton $\{a\}$ when $a = b$.
- $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are nonempty exactly when $a < b$, and then each
  is nondegenerate.

The only assertion here that is not immediate from the defining conditions is
that $a < b$ makes $(a,b)$ nonempty with at least two points. It holds because
$a < (a+b)/2 < b$, which follows from $a < b$ by adding $a$, respectively $b$, to
both sides and halving ([[def-ordered-field]]); repeating the halving inside
$(a, (a+b)/2)$ produces a second point.

**Closed bounded intervals.** These are the sets $[a,b]$ with $a \le b$, which is
exactly the condition making them nonempty. They are the intervals the nested
interval property is stated for, and the phrase *closed bounded interval* always
carries the hypothesis $a \le b$ in this library.

**Length.** The **length** of a bounded interval presented by its endpoints
$a \le b$ is

$$\ell = b - a \;\ge\; 0 .$$

Length is attached to the presentation by endpoints and is not recovered from the
set: $(a,b)$, $[a,b)$ and $(a,b]$ are all empty when $a = b$, and so is
$(c,c)$ for any other $c$, while each of these presentations has length $0$, so
nothing inconsistent arises; but the endpoints are named explicitly at every
point where a length is used in this library, and never inferred from the set.
Unbounded intervals are assigned no length.

Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a > 0$ and let $r \in \mathbb{Q}$ ([[def-rationals]]).

Every rational has a representative with positive denominator
([[lem-rat-positive-denominator]]), so write $r = m/n$ with $m \in \mathbb{Z}$
and $n$ a positive integer; a positive integer is the image of a unique natural
$\ge 1$ ([[lem-nat-embeds-int]]), and we write $n$ for that natural too. Define

$$a^{r} := \big(a^{1/n}\big)^{m},$$

where $a^{1/n}$ is the unique nonnegative $n$-th root of $a$
([[thm-nth-roots-exist]]) and the outer exponent is an integer power
([[def-integer-power]]). The outer power is legitimate because $a^{1/n} > 0$ when
$a > 0$, so it has an inverse and negative integer exponents are allowed.

**Well-definedness.** The right-hand side must not depend on which representative
$m/n$ of $r$ was chosen. It does not: that is [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]],
which is recorded in this item's `justified_by` rather than in its `deps`, since
it is a statement *about* the operation defined here and therefore depends on
this definition.

**The base must be positive.** For $a < 0$ the same formula is not a definition
at all, because different representatives of the same rational give different
answers, or no answer: see [[fs-rational-power-of-negative-base]], which is
exactly the item that justifies the restriction.

**Supplementary clause for the base $0$.** For $a = 0$ and rational $r > 0$
([[def-rat-order]]) the displayed formula still makes sense and still does not
depend on the representative: $r > 0$ forces $m \ge 1$, and
$\big(0^{1/n}\big)^{m} = 0^{m} = 0$ ([[thm-nth-roots-exist]] applies to every
$a \ge 0$). So we set $0^{r} = 0$ for rational $r > 0$. For $r < 0$ the
expression $0^{r}$ is left undefined, since $0$ has no inverse. This clause is
what lets the inequalities later on this page be stated for nonnegative entries
rather than for positive ones only.

derivations.claim: (The worldline.) By [L4], $\eta(v,v)=-1$ and $v^0>0$, so $U_0=c\,v$ satisfies $g_p(U_0,U_0)=c^2\eta(v,v)=-c^2$ by [L1] and is future timelike. By [L2] the maximal geodesic with $x(\gamma(0))=0$ and velocity $v$ has $x(\gamma(s))=s\,v$ on $\mathbb R$ and is a future timelike worldline; its speed is the constant $\eta(v,v)=-1$; and $\tau(s)=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}\,(s-0)/c=s/c$ is proper time up to an additive constant, with $d\gamma/d\tau=c\,v=U_0$ and $g(d\gamma/d\tau,d\gamma/d\tau)=c^2\eta(v,v)=-c^2$.

(Coordinate velocity.) In the parametrization $x(\gamma(t))=(ct,\mathbf q(t))$ of [L2] clause (e), the coordinate velocity is $\mathbf w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)=(\sqrt3/2)\,c\,(1/\sqrt3,0,0)=(c/2,0,0)$ using [L4]; hence $|\mathbf w|=c/2<c$ and $1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2=1-1/4=3/4$, so $\sqrt{1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2}=\sqrt3/2$.

(Clock reading via the proper-time density.) Parametrize the worldline by $t=x^0/c$; its tangent is $\gamma'_t=(c,\mathbf w)$ with components $(c,c/2,0,0)$, so by [L1] $g(\gamma'_t,\gamma'_t)=c^2(-1+1/4)=-3c^2/4$ and [L3] gives $\tau'(t)=\tfrac1c\sqrt{3c^2/4}=\sqrt3/2>0$. Integrating over $[t_0,t_1]$ gives $\Delta\tau=(t_1-t_0)\sqrt3/2=\sqrt{1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2}\,(t_1-t_0)$ by step 1.2.

(Cross-check with the affine parametrization.) On the parametrization $\gamma(s)=sv$ one has $x^0(\gamma(s))=sv^0$, that is $t=v^0s/c$, and step 1.1 identifies $\tau=s/c$, so $\tau=t/v^0=(\sqrt3/2)\,t$ by [L4]; hence between $t_0$ and $t_1$ the elapsed proper time is $(t_1-t_0)/v^0=(t_1-t_0)\sqrt3/2$, in agreement with step 2.1. The identity $1/v^0=\sqrt{1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2}$ is exactly $\eta(v,v)=-1$: $1-|\mathbf w|^2/c^2=1-|v^1|^2/(v^0)^2=(1+|v^1|^2-|v^1|^2)/(v^0)^2=1/(v^0)^2$.

boundaries.reason: The curve, the interval [t0,t1] and the vector v are nonempty fixed data.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.2 computes the coordinate velocity w and step 3.1 the clock identity; the case w = 0 is the limit of the same formulas and the identity 1/v0 = sqrt(1-|w|²/c²) holds with equality; no separate degenerate branch is needed.

step 2.1 integrates the proper-time density over [t0,t1] and step 3.1 compares with the direct parametrization t = v0τ, so both time endpoints are disposed of.

The example verifies identities; it asserts no equivalence.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, and let $n$ be an observer at $p$
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,
$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,n)=0\}$
([[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]) and
$\mathbb Rn=\{\lambda n:\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$. Then:

1. $h:T_pM\to T_pM$ is linear, $h(n)=0$, $h(v)=v$ for every $v\in n^{\perp}$
   and $h\circ h=h$; its kernel is $\ker h=\mathbb Rn$, its image is
   $\operatorname{im}h=n^{\perp}$, and
   $T_pM=\mathbb Rn\oplus n^{\perp}$ is an orthogonal direct sum: every
   $v\in T_pM$ has the unique decomposition

   $$v=-g_p(v,n)\,n+h(v),$$

   in which $-g_p(v,n)n\in\mathbb Rn$ and $h(v)\in n^{\perp}$.
2. For all $v,w\in T_pM$ the **projection identity**

   $$g_p(h(v),h(w))=g_p(v,w)+g_p(v,n)g_p(n,w)$$

   holds; in particular $g_p(h(v),h(v))=g_p(v,v)+g_p(v,n)^2$.
3. $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive
   definite.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, let $n$ be an observer at $p$, and let $c>0$ be a real parameter
([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observer energy and spatial momentum.** For every $P\in T_pM$ define the
**observer energy** and the **spatial momentum** of $P$ relative to $n$ by

$$E_n(P):=-c\,g_p(P,n),\qquad q_n(P):=h_n(P),$$

where $h_n$ is the spatial projection of the observer $n$. Both maps are
$\mathbb R$-linear in $P$: the first because $g_p$ is bilinear, the second by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The second takes values in the
rest space $n^{\perp}$, and by the rest-space decomposition of that lemma every
$P$ has the unique decomposition

$$P=\frac{E_n(P)}{c}\,n+q_n(P),\qquad \frac{E_n(P)}{c}\in\mathbb R,\quad q_n(P)\in n^{\perp}.$$

Equivalently $E_n(P)=c\,\lambda$ and $q_n(P)=w$ for the unique pair
$(\lambda,w)$ with $P=\lambda n+w$, $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, $w\in n^{\perp}$.

**(b) Rest mass and four-velocity normalization.** For $P\in T_pM$ with
$g_p(P,P)\le0$ define the **rest mass**

$$m(P):=\frac{\sqrt{-g_p(P,P)}}{c}\ge0,$$

where the square root is the nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]. By
strict positivity of the square root of a positive number, $m(P)=0$ exactly
when $P=0$ or $P$ is null, and $m(P)>0$ exactly when $P$ is timelike
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). When $m(P)>0$, define the
**normalized four-velocity direction**

$$U(P):=\frac{P}{m(P)},$$

so that $g_p(U(P),U(P))=g_p(P,P)/m(P)^2=-c^2$. Conversely, if $m>0$ and
$U\in T_pM$ satisfy $g_p(U,U)=-c^2$, then $P:=mU$ has $g_p(P,P)=-m^2c^2$ and
$m(P)=m$, $U(P)=U$; the pair $(m,U)$ with $U$ future-directed determines and
is determined by its future timelike $P=mU$.

**(c) Scope and reading.** $E_n$ and $q_n$ depend on the observer $n$: for the
same nonzero $P$, different observers $n,n'$ generally give different values,
and no observer-independent splitting of $P$ into "energy" and "momentum" is
defined by this item. The identities above are algebraic; this definition
asserts no positivity of $E_n$ (that is proved separately), no conservation,
no dynamics and no measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum
and rest mass, and their physical units and interpretation, belong to the
physical reading of the framework's unit conventions and postulates and are
not asserted here; this item fixes only the mathematical dependence on the
objects $P$, $n$, $g_p$ and the parameter $c$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$p\in M$, let $n$ be an observer at $p$, let $c>0$, and for
$P\in T_pM$ write $E:=E_n(P)$ and $q:=q_n(P)$ as in
[[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]. When $g_p(P,P)\le0$, also
write $m:=m(P)=\sqrt{-g_p(P,P)}/c$; $m(P)$ is not defined for spacelike $P$. Then:

1. **Master identity.** $E^2=c^2\bigl(g_p(q,q)-g_p(P,P)\bigr)$.
2. **Positivity.** If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E>0$.
3. **Mass shell.** If $P$ is future timelike, then $m>0$ and, with
   $U:=P/m$, $u:=U/c$ and $\gamma:=-g_p(n,u)$, one has $\gamma\ge1$,
   $E=mc^2\gamma$, $q=m\gamma w$ where $w:=c\,h_n(u)/\gamma$,
   $g_p(q,q)=m^2c^2(\gamma^2-1)$ and

   $$E^2=m^2c^4+c^2g_p(q,q).$$
4. **Null case.** If $P$ is future null and nonzero, then $E>0$,
   $E=c\sqrt{g_p(q,q)}$ and $E^2=c^2g_p(q,q)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, $p\in M$,
$n$ an observer at $p$ and $P\in T_pM$ a future timelike vector with rest
mass $m:=m(P)>0$ ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]],
[[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $U:=P/m$, $u:=U/c$,
$\gamma:=-g_p(n,u)$ and, as in clause 3 of
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-identities]],

$$w:=\frac{c\,h_n(u)}{\gamma}\in n^\perp,\qquad s:=\sqrt{g_p(w,w)} .$$

For $z\in n^\perp$ write $|z|_n:=\sqrt{g_p(z,z)}$, the norm from the positive-definite restriction of $g_p$ to $n^\perp$. Thus $s=|w|_n$, and $|q_n(P)|$ in the displays below means $|q_n(P)|_n$; $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ by the observer decomposition.

Then $s<c$, $\gamma=(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$,

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2},\qquad |q_n(P)|=ms\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2},$$

and for every $0\le v_0<c$, with $z_0:=v_0^2/c^2<1$ and all $s\le v_0$,

$$\Bigl|E_n(P)-mc^2-\tfrac12ms^2\Bigr|\le\tfrac38\,(1-z_0)^{-5/2}\,\frac{ms^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl||q_n(P)|-ms\Bigr|\le\tfrac12\,(1-z_0)^{-3/2}\,\frac{ms^3}{c^2} .$$

Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ carry its standard smooth structure
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and let
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ be the **identity chart**, $x(p)=p$;
it is a global chart of the maximal smooth atlas, and the coordinate
derivations $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ form a basis of
$T_pM$ at every $p\in M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). Write

$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$$

for the standard Lorentz form of inertia $(3,1,0)$ in this basis
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

**(a) The metric.** Define the covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$ by the
requirement that its components in the identity chart are the constants

$$g_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}\qquad(a,b=0,1,2,3),$$

that is, $g_p(\partial_a|_p,\partial_b|_p)=\eta_{ab}$ for every $p\in M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] clause (a)). The component
functions are constant, hence $C^\infty$, so $g$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field; at every $p$ the form $g_p$ is nondegenerate with
inertia $(3,1,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a) the
pair $(M,g)$ is therefore a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$.

**(b) The inertial chart and frame.** The chart $x$ is called the **inertial
chart** of the flat model. In this chart the coordinate frame
$(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is a $g$-orthonormal frame at
every point, $g(\partial_a,\partial_b)=\eta_{ab}$; it is simultaneously a
coordinate frame and a **tetrad field** in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], defined on all of $M$.

**(c) Time orientation and causal classification.** Define the smooth vector
field $N:=\partial_0$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)=\eta_{00}=-1<0$ for every $p$, the field $N$ is everywhere
timelike, so $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). For a nonzero tangent
vector $v=v^a\partial_a|_p$ the definitions of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c) and
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] give

$$g_p(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2,\qquad g_p(v,N_p)=-v^0 .$$

so $v$ is **future-directed** exactly when $v^0>0$, and

- $v$ is future timelike $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2>\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is future null $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2=\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is spacelike $\iff$ $(v^0)^2<\sum_i(v^i)^2$;

consequently the future causal cone at every point is
$\{v\neq0: v^0\ge\sqrt{\sum_i(v^i)^2}\}$. These are the standard readings of
the Minkowski form in the inertial chart; the chain of equivalences is the
specialization of the causal classification to this pair $(g_p,N_p)$ and is
recorded here for later use.

**(d) Scope.** This item defines geometric data only: a manifold, a metric
field, a time orientation and a distinguished chart and frame. It makes no
claim about curvature, about any field equation, about which geometry a
physical model uses, or about nature; the physical reading of the data, the
dimensions of the coordinates and the numerical values or signs of physical
constants belong to the framework's unit conventions and postulates, which
are separate items. In particular no relation between the coordinate
functions $x^a$ and physical time or length measurements is asserted here.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Let $a \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a > 0$ and let $r \in \mathbb{Q}$ ([[def-rationals]]).

Every rational has a representative with positive denominator
([[lem-rat-positive-denominator]]), so write $r = m/n$ with $m \in \mathbb{Z}$
and $n$ a positive integer; a positive integer is the image of a unique natural
$\ge 1$ ([[lem-nat-embeds-int]]), and we write $n$ for that natural too. Define

$$a^{r} := \big(a^{1/n}\big)^{m},$$

where $a^{1/n}$ is the unique nonnegative $n$-th root of $a$
([[thm-nth-roots-exist]]) and the outer exponent is an integer power
([[def-integer-power]]). The outer power is legitimate because $a^{1/n} > 0$ when
$a > 0$, so it has an inverse and negative integer exponents are allowed.

**Well-definedness.** The right-hand side must not depend on which representative
$m/n$ of $r$ was chosen. It does not: that is [[lem-rational-power-well-defined]],
which is recorded in this item's `justified_by` rather than in its `deps`, since
it is a statement *about* the operation defined here and therefore depends on
this definition.

**The base must be positive.** For $a < 0$ the same formula is not a definition
at all, because different representatives of the same rational give different
answers, or no answer: see [[fs-rational-power-of-negative-base]], which is
exactly the item that justifies the restriction.

**Supplementary clause for the base $0$.** For $a = 0$ and rational $r > 0$
([[def-rat-order]]) the displayed formula still makes sense and still does not
depend on the representative: $r > 0$ forces $m \ge 1$, and
$\big(0^{1/n}\big)^{m} = 0^{m} = 0$ ([[thm-nth-roots-exist]] applies to every
$a \ge 0$). So we set $0^{r} = 0$ for rational $r > 0$. For $r < 0$ the
expression $0^{r}$ is left undefined, since $0$ has no inverse. This clause is
what lets the inequalities later on this page be stated for nonnegative entries
rather than for positive ones only.

derivations.claim: (Observer data.) By [L4], $g_p(n,n)=-1$, so $n$ is a unit future-directed timelike vector, i.e. an observer. Set $u$ as given; then $g_p(u,u)=\frac{4}{3}g_p(\partial_0,\partial_0)+\frac13g_p(\partial_1,\partial_1)=-\frac43+\frac13=-1$, so $u$ is future timelike with $g_p(u,u)=-1$, and $P=mcu$ is future timelike with rest mass $m(P)=m$ by [L2]. Further $g_p(n,u)=-\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$, so by [L1] $h_n(u)=u+g_p(n,u)n=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\partial_0+\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\partial_1-\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\partial_0=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\partial_1$. Hence $\gamma=-g_p(n,u)=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\ge1$, $w=c\,h_n(u)/\gamma=\frac{c}{2}\partial_1$, and $s=\sqrt{g_p(w,w)}=\frac c2$ by [L4].

(Exact energy and momentum.) By [L2] and [L4]: $E_n(P)=-cg_p(P,n)=-m c^2\,g_p(u,\partial_0)=mc^2\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$ and $q_n(P)=h_n(P)=mc\,h_n(u)=\frac{mc}{\sqrt3}\partial_1$, so $|q_n(P)|=\sqrt{g_p(q_n,q_n)}=\frac{mc}{\sqrt3}$ since $g_p(\partial_1,\partial_1)=1$.

(Exact identities at $s=c/2$.) By step 1.1, $s=c/2<c$ and $1-s^2/c^2=3/4$, so $(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}=2/\sqrt3$; step 2.1 gives $E_n(P)=mc^2\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=mc^2(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and $|q_n(P)|=\frac{mc}{\sqrt3}=m\cdot\frac c2\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=ms(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, which are the exact identities of [L3].

(Energy bound.) By step 3.1, $\bigl|E_n(P)-mc^2-\frac12ms^2\bigr|=mc^2\bigl|\frac{2}{\sqrt3}-1-\frac18\bigr|=mc^2\bigl(\frac{2}{\sqrt3}-\frac98\bigr)=mc^2\,\frac{16-9\sqrt3}{8\sqrt3}$, the sign being positive by [L5]. The bound of [L3] at $v_0=c/2$ is $\frac38\bigl(\frac34\bigr)^{-5/2}m\frac{(c/2)^4}{c^2}=\frac{3}{8}\cdot\frac{32}{9\sqrt3}\cdot\frac{mc^2}{16}=\frac{mc^2}{12\sqrt3}$ using $(\frac43)^{5/2}=\frac{16}{9}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$ and $\sqrt3>0$. The inequality $\frac{16-9\sqrt3}{8\sqrt3}\le\frac{1}{12\sqrt3}$ is equivalent, upon multiplying by the positive $24\sqrt3$, to $3(16-9\sqrt3)\le2$, i.e. $27\sqrt3\ge46$, which holds by [L5].

(Momentum bound.) By step 3.1, $\bigl||q_n(P)|-ms\bigr|=mc\bigl|\frac{1}{\sqrt3}-\frac12\bigr|=mc\bigl(\frac{1}{\sqrt3}-\frac12\bigr)=mc\,\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2\sqrt3}$ by [L5]. The bound of [L3] at $v_0=c/2$ is $\frac12\bigl(\frac34\bigr)^{-3/2}m\frac{(c/2)^3}{c^2}=\frac12\cdot\frac{8}{3\sqrt3}\cdot\frac{mc}{8}=\frac{mc}{6\sqrt3}$ using $(\frac43)^{3/2}=\frac43\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$. The inequality $\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2\sqrt3}\le\frac{1}{6\sqrt3}$ is equivalent, upon multiplying by the positive $6\sqrt3$, to $3(2-\sqrt3)\le1$, i.e. $3\sqrt3\ge5$, which holds since $27>25$ and both sides are positive. Both bounds of the lemma are therefore satisfied strictly at the relative speed $s=c/2$, and the exact identities of step 3.1 verify its statements $s<c$, $\gamma=(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ and the two displayed formulas. [step 3.1, step 4.1, L3, L5, algebra] ∎



- **Scope.** The example is a finite algebraic check of the kinematic identities and error bounds at one relative speed; it involves no dynamics, no conservation law and no measurement. The choices $s=c/2$ and the direction $\partial_1$ are arbitrary normalizations; the points checked are the exact identities and the two strict inequalities.

boundaries.evidence: step 3.1 and step 4.1 compare nonzero exact values with the bounds; the zero case is the exact identity at s = 0 for the same formulas, and the strict inequalities at s = c/2 are consistent with the vanishing error at s = 0.

boundaries.reason: The computation is four-dimensional at a single point; no one-dimensional case is asserted.

s=v0=c/2 is the included endpoint of the lemma speed range, with z0=1/4<1.

The example checks identities and inequalities; no equivalence is asserted.
The check verifies the lemma's identities and bounds at one relative speed; it asserts no converse direction such as sharpness of the bounds.

Both strict comparisons reduce to positive squaring: 2187>2116 and 27>25. The stated example is unchanged; s=v0=c/2 is the included endpoint of the lemma speed range. No measured numbers or sharpness claim.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g_\eta,N_\eta)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and constant components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be a
nonempty open spacetime region, identified with its image in $\mathbb R^4$,
and let $\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be the spatial projection
$\pi(x^0,\mathbf x)=\mathbf x$. Its image $U:=\pi(\Omega)$ is open: a
coordinate ball in $\Omega$ about any point projects onto a ball about that
point's spatial coordinates. Let $K\subseteq U$ be compact. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N>0$ be the constants of the framework's conventions and put
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The coordinates have units of metres, $c$ has units
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ is dimensionless.

**(a) Structural data.** A tuple $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is
**stationary weak-field data** when

- $L>0$ is a length, $C>0$ is dimensionless, and $\varepsilon_0>0$ is
  dimensionless;
- $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth dimensionless spatial function and
  $r=(r_{ab})$ is a family of smooth dimensionless spatial functions
  $r_{ab}:(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times U\to\mathbb R$ for some
  $\varepsilon_1>\varepsilon_0$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]);
- for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)=\begin{cases}-(1+2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))+r_{00}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=b=0,\\[2pt] r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&\{a,b\}=\{0,i\},\\[2pt] (1-2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))\,\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=i,\ b=j,\end{cases}$$

  is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\varepsilon)$ on
  $\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
- **(spatial factorization and stationarity)** all metric components factor
  through $\pi$ by construction. Thus points of $\Omega$ with the same
  spatial coordinates have the same metric components, even when they lie in
  different connected components of that spatial fiber, and
  $\partial_0g_{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$;
- **(spatial bounds)** for every multiindex $\alpha\in\mathbb N^3$ with
  $|\alpha|\le2$ and every $\mathbf x\in K$,

$$|\partial^\alpha\varphi(\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{00}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|+|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^{|\alpha|}}.$$

  (Derivatives are with respect to $x^1,x^2,x^3$; here $|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}|$
  is the maximum over $i,j$ and $|\partial^\alpha r_{0i}|$ is the maximum
  over $i$.)

**(b) Derived data.** For stationary weak-field data define the
**spatial potential**

$$\Phi:=\varepsilon c^2\varphi\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a smooth spatial function of dimension $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ in the
framework's unit conventions; its pullback to $\Omega$ is stationary. The
symmetric component family $g(\varepsilon)-\eta$ is the **perturbation of the
family**.

**(c) Einstein families.** Stationary weak-field data form an **Einstein
family with coupling $\kappa$** when for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$
there is a smooth symmetric component field $T_{ab}(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ on
$\Omega$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) satisfying

$$G_{ab}\bigl(g(\varepsilon)\bigr)=\kappa\,T_{ab}(\varepsilon)\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection of
$g(\varepsilon)$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). In that case define the
**spatial density read from the time-time component**

$$\rho_\varepsilon(\mathbf x):=\frac{T_{00}(\varepsilon,x^0,\mathbf x)}{c^2}\qquad\text{on }U,$$

where any $x^0$ with $(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\Omega$ may be used. This is
well-defined: the metric is the pullback of spatial functions, so its
coordinate curvature components, and hence $T_{00}=\kappa^{-1}G_{00}$, are
constant on each fiber of $\pi$, including when that fiber is disconnected.
It has units $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; it is a coordinate-component
density and is not thereby the dust rest-mass density.

**(d) Scope.** This item fixes a class of metric families and the vocabulary
of the weak-field bridge: the spatial factorization, component form,
stationarity, spatial derivative bounds, potential, and the equation that
upgrades the data to an Einstein family. It asserts neither existence for prescribed data nor that $\partial_0$ is
timelike or a Killing field, that the inverse metrics are uniformly bounded,
or that $\rho_\varepsilon$ is positive; the latter properties are
consequences proved separately where they are used. The family is an explicit
input-family hypothesis: neither its existence for prescribed Newtonian
initial data nor its construction from other data is claimed. The physical
reading of the components, of $G_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$, of $\Phi$ and of
$\rho_\varepsilon$ belongs to the framework's postulates and unit
conventions, which are separate items.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$ and compact $K\subseteq U$, and suppose the
data form an Einstein family with coupling $\kappa>0$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]] clauses (a)-(c)). Write
$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$,
$\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2:U\to\mathbb R$, and let $G^{(1)}$ be the
first-order Einstein coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N:=\kappa c^4/(8\pi)$. There are $\varepsilon_*'>0$, depending only on $\varepsilon_0$, $C$,
$L$ and the dimension, and $C_2<\infty$, depending only on $C$, $L$ and
the dimension, such that for every
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*'$ the following inequalities hold at every
spacetime point $p\in\Omega$ with $\pi(p)\in K$. Spatial derivatives and
$\Delta$ are taken on $U$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), and maxima
are over the free component indices.

**(a) Linearized approximation.** With
$A_{ab}(\varepsilon):=g_{ab}(\varepsilon)-\eta_{ab}$,

$$\bigl|G_{ab}(g(\varepsilon))-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A(\varepsilon))\bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2} .$$

**(b) Component hierarchy of the Einstein tensor.**

$$\Bigl|G_{00}(g(\varepsilon))-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{ij}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{0i}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

**(c) Stress hierarchy and independent dust source.** The Einstein equation
gives

$$\Bigl|\kappa T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{ij}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{0i}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

For every Einstein family, the definition $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$ therefore gives
$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\rho_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{2L^2}.$$

For the additional conclusion below, let $\nabla^\varepsilon$ denote the
metric-selected connection of $g(\varepsilon)$ and assume the Einstein source is an
**independent admissible nonnegative dust input**: for each $\varepsilon$,
there are smooth fields $\mathcal E_\varepsilon:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ and
$u_\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, with $u_\varepsilon$ future-directed and
$g(\varepsilon)(u_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)=-1$, such that
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon (u_\varepsilon)_a(u_\varepsilon)_b$ and
$$\nabla^\varepsilon_a(\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_\varepsilon^a)=0,\qquad u_\varepsilon^a\nabla^\varepsilon_a u_\varepsilon^b=0 .$$
Where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon>0$, this is the dust model of
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; where it vanishes, the smooth field
$u_\varepsilon$ remains specified and satisfies the geodesic equation by
the explicit hypotheses above. The stress
conservation identity follows from these equations (and agrees on the
positive-density region with [[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]).
No comoving condition is imposed: the spatial tilt may be nonzero.
Define the independent rest-mass density
$$\mu_\varepsilon:=\mathcal E_\varepsilon/c^2\quad[\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}],$$
where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ has the rest-energy-density unit
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mu_\varepsilon$ is independent of the
coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon$.
It factors through $\pi$: normalization gives $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=-g^{ab}T_{ab}=-\kappa^{-1}g^{ab}G_{ab}$, whose components factor through the spatial projection by the Einstein-family hypothesis. Thus $\mu_\varepsilon$ also denotes its resulting smooth spatial function on $U$, including on disconnected fibers.
On $K$, assume the explicit weak-source and tilted slow-motion bounds
$$0\le\mathcal E_\varepsilon\le\frac{C\varepsilon c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad s_\varepsilon\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\,c,$$
where on the region over $K$ the time orientation is chosen so that
$\partial_0$ is future (and $g(u_\varepsilon,\partial_0)<0$), and
$n_\varepsilon:=\partial_0/\sqrt{-g_{00}}$ is the resulting future unit
coordinate observer, $\gamma_\varepsilon:=-g(u_\varepsilon,n_\varepsilon)$,
$h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon):=u_\varepsilon+g(n_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)n_\varepsilon$,
and $s_\varepsilon$ is the norm of
$c\,h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)/\gamma_\varepsilon$ in the observer's
rest space ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
[[lem-gr-observer-relative-velocity-expansions]]). Choose
$$\varepsilon_*'\le\min\{\varepsilon_0,1,(128C)^{-1},(4C^2)^{-1}\},$$
also small enough for the two-jet estimate in the proof. This threshold
condition is dimensionless.
Then, for a constant $C_d$ depending only on $C$,

$$|T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\mu_\varepsilon c^2|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad |\rho_\varepsilon-\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^2}{G_NL^2},$$

and the distinct dust rest-mass density satisfies the Poisson estimate

$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{L^2} .$$

The energy- and mass-density conventions of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
give the same tensor here:
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_a u_b=c^2\mu_\varepsilon u_a u_b$,
with $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=c^2\mu_\varepsilon$.

**(d) Scaled dust source.** Let $X:=\mathbf x/L$ and
$U_L:=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$. Define
$\psi(X):=\varphi(LX)$ and
$R(X):=G_NL^2\mu_\varepsilon(LX)/(\varepsilon c^2)$ on $U_L$, with
$\Delta_X$ the Laplacian in $X$. Then

$$|\Delta_X\psi-4\pi R|\le C_2\varepsilon\qquad\text{on }K/L .$$

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Then $\nabla f$ is a $C^1$ field on $U$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], since each of its components $\partial_if$ has continuous first partial derivatives, so its divergence is defined; the **Laplacian** of $f$ is

$$\Delta f:=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_{i<n}\partial_i\partial_if,$$

with the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. A $C^2$ function with $\Delta f=0$ on $U$ is called **harmonic** on $U$.

For a $C^2$ map $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{q-1}):U\to\mathbb R^q$, whose components are $C^2$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], $\Delta F$ is the field whose $i$th coordinate is $\Delta F_i$. In the three-coordinate naming of this page, $\Delta f=\partial_x\partial_xf+\partial_y\partial_yf+\partial_z\partial_zf$ and $\Delta F=(\Delta F_x,\Delta F_y,\Delta F_z)$.

Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open set of the flat model
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]], let
$(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over $\Omega$ with
first-order coefficients $\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$, $S^{(1)}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}$ and with trace
reversal $\bar h$, d'Alembertian $\Box$ and gauge transformation
$h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ as in
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], and let $L>0$ be a length scale.
All components are taken in the inertial chart and all contractions are
with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$.

**(a) Christoffel symbols.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there is a
constant $C_K<\infty$ such that for all $p\in K$ and
$0<|\lambda|\le\varepsilon_1/2$,

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,\eta^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bh_{cd}+\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(b) Ricci tensor.** With the same constants (enlarged if necessary),

$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** In this clause, suprema of the nonnegative
component magnitudes over an empty set are defined to be $0$. For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

derivations.claim: (Admissible data.) The fields are smooth and factor through the spatial projection. For $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$ and $\mathbf x\in U$, $0\le2\varepsilon\varphi<1/2$, so [L5] gives a diagonal Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on all of $\Omega$. On $K$, $|\varphi|\le1/8$, $|\partial_i\varphi|\le1/(2L)$ and $|\partial_i\partial_j\varphi|\le1/L^2$, so the bounds hold with $C=1$; $r=0$ satisfies its bounds on $(-\varepsilon_1^{\mathrm{data}},\varepsilon_1^{\mathrm{data}})$, with $\varepsilon_1^{\mathrm{data}}=1>\varepsilon_0=1/2$. Taking $\delta_1=1/2$ and $q=0$ gives the stated flat linearized family.

(First-order coefficient.) By [L3], $\Delta\varphi=3/L^2$. The trace reversal has $\bar h_{00}=-4\varphi$ and all other components zero. Formula [L4], stationarity and $\Box=\Delta$ give $G^{(1)}_{00}(h)=2\Delta\varphi=6/L^2$ and $G^{(1)}_{0i}(h)=G^{(1)}_{ij}(h)=0$. Linearity gives $G^{(1)}_{00}(A(\varepsilon))=6\varepsilon/L^2$ and the remaining displayed components vanish.

(Einstein family.) Define $T_{ab}(\varepsilon)=G_{ab}(g(\varepsilon))/\kappa$ on $\Omega$. The metric-selected connection and curvature depend smoothly on the metric and its derivatives; hence $T$ is a smooth symmetric component field and $G=\kappa T$ identically. Thus the data are an Einstein family by [L1], with coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$. This construction is a mathematical source prescription, not a dust realization.

(Exact Poisson source and coordinate-density estimate.) By [L3], $\Delta\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\Delta\varphi=3\varepsilon c^2/L^2$. Defining $\bar\rho=3\varepsilon c^2/(4\pi G_NL^2)$ gives $\Delta\Phi=4\pi G_N\bar\rho$ exactly. By [L2], [step 2.1, L2, L3, L5, algebra]
$$|\kappa c^2\rho_\varepsilon-6\varepsilon/L^2|\le C_2\varepsilon^2/L^2.$$
Since $\kappa c^2\bar\rho=6\varepsilon/L^2$ and $\kappa c^2=8\pi G_N/c^2$, division by $\kappa c^2>0$ gives
$$|\rho_\varepsilon-\bar\rho|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{8\pi G_NL^2}.$$
This compares the exact Newtonian source with the relativistic coordinate density to the order established by the component hierarchy; it does not assert equality or an independent dust source.
(Leading term.) By steps 1.2 and 3.1, $G^{(1)}_{00}(A(\varepsilon))=6\varepsilon/L^2=2\Delta\Phi/c^2$, and the other first-order Einstein components vanish as stated. This completes the verification.

boundaries.reason: Ω is the nonempty unit ball and K the nonempty closed ball of radius 1/2; no empty set arises.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 verifies the bounds at the origin and step 3.1 evaluates ΔΦ = 3εc²; the potential vanishes at x = 0, which is the interior minimum included in the bounds |φ| ≤ 1/8.

boundaries.reason: The dimension is four; no one-dimensional specialization is claimed.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 checks |2εφ| < 1/2 on Ω for 0 < |ε| ≤ 1/2, so the metric stays Lorentzian and the degenerate smallness boundary is excluded explicitly.

boundaries.reason: All bounds are on the fixed compact K and for 0 < ε ≤ ε_*'; no interval endpoint value is asserted.
The constants L, C, ε0 and the density are fixed explicitly; no selection occurs.
The example exhibits data and computes dictionary quantities; no equivalence is asserted.
No converse (for example uniqueness of the density) is claimed.

risk_review.notes: Accepted distinct remainder-domain parameter 1>epsilon0=1/2 and linearization radius delta1=1/2. Verified metric signs on BL for both signed linearization parameters and positive stationary parameters including epsilon0, derivative bounds on BL/2, Delta phi=3/L^2, and G1_00=6epsilon/L^2. T=G/kappa gives a smooth symmetric Einstein family without dust; general hierarchy only gives coordinate-density estimate after dividing kappa c^2=8pi GN/c^2. No misuse of independent-dust conclusion. Actual hierarchy threshold is used, so dependence correction needs no consumer text change.

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g_\eta,N_\eta)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and constant components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be a
nonempty open spacetime region, identified with its image in $\mathbb R^4$,
and let $\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be the spatial projection
$\pi(x^0,\mathbf x)=\mathbf x$. Its image $U:=\pi(\Omega)$ is open: a
coordinate ball in $\Omega$ about any point projects onto a ball about that
point's spatial coordinates. Let $K\subseteq U$ be compact. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N>0$ be the constants of the framework's conventions and put
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The coordinates have units of metres, $c$ has units
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ is dimensionless.

**(a) Structural data.** A tuple $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is
**stationary weak-field data** when

- $L>0$ is a length, $C>0$ is dimensionless, and $\varepsilon_0>0$ is
  dimensionless;
- $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth dimensionless spatial function and
  $r=(r_{ab})$ is a family of smooth dimensionless spatial functions
  $r_{ab}:(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times U\to\mathbb R$ for some
  $\varepsilon_1>\varepsilon_0$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]);
- for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)=\begin{cases}-(1+2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))+r_{00}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=b=0,\\[2pt] r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&\{a,b\}=\{0,i\},\\[2pt] (1-2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))\,\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=i,\ b=j,\end{cases}$$

  is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\varepsilon)$ on
  $\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
- **(spatial factorization and stationarity)** all metric components factor
  through $\pi$ by construction. Thus points of $\Omega$ with the same
  spatial coordinates have the same metric components, even when they lie in
  different connected components of that spatial fiber, and
  $\partial_0g_{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$;
- **(spatial bounds)** for every multiindex $\alpha\in\mathbb N^3$ with
  $|\alpha|\le2$ and every $\mathbf x\in K$,

$$|\partial^\alpha\varphi(\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{00}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|+|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^{|\alpha|}}.$$
