**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: (The action.) In the chart $x$ the action reads $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\mapsto(x^0+nL,x^1,x^2,x^3)$; each $p\mapsto n\cdot p$ is a smooth translation, so the action is smooth; it is an action of the group $\mathbb Z$ on $\hat M$ with $0\cdot p=p$ and $(n+m)\cdot p=n\cdot(m\cdot p)$. It is free: $n\cdot p=p$ forces $nL=0$, hence $n=0$. It preserves $\hat g$: the differential of a translation in the chart is the identity, so $\hat g_{n\cdot p}(d(n\cdot)_pV,d(n\cdot)_pW)=\hat g_p(V,W)$ by [L1]. It is proper: if $K_1,K_2\subseteq\hat M$ are compact and $p\in K_1$ with $n\cdot p\in K_2$, then $|n|L\le\sup_{K_1}|x^0|+\sup_{K_2}|x^0|<\infty$ by [L8], so only finitely many $n$ occur; hence $\Theta^{-1}(K_1\times K_2)$ is a finite union of compact sets, one for each such $n$, and is compact. Finally $\hat N=\partial_0$ is $\Gamma$-invariant with $\hat g(\hat N,\hat N)=-1<0$, since it is invariant under translations.

(The smooth quotient.) By step 1.1, [L2] and the zero-dimensional Lie-group structure of [L3], $M$ is a Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold and $q$ is a smooth surjective submersion. Thus $dq_p$ is onto between four-dimensional tangent spaces and hence invertible for every $p$. The inverse function theorem in [L2] gives a local diffeomorphism $q|_{\hat U}:\hat U\to V$ at each point, with smooth inverse $s:V\to\hat U$. The quotient is connected as the image of connected $\hat M$ under the continuous surjection $q$.

(Metric and time orientation.) For $r=q(p)$ and $v,w\in T_rM$ define $g_r(v,w):=\hat g_p((dq_p)^{-1}v,(dq_p)^{-1}w)$ and $N_r:=dq_p(\hat N_p)$. These definitions are independent of the representative: if $p'=n\cdot p$, differentiating $q\circ(n\cdot)=q$ gives $dq_{p'}\circ d(n\cdot)_p=dq_p$, so the inverse images of $v,w$ at $p'$ are the translates of those at $p$. Metric invariance and field invariance from step 1.1 therefore give the same values for $g_r$ and $N_r$. The form $g_r$ is symmetric and nondegenerate with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ because $dq_p$ is invertible and $\hat g_p$ has that signature. Over every inverse section $s$ of step 2.1 one has $g|_V=s^*\hat g$ and $N_r=dq_{s(r)}(\hat N_{s(r)})$, both smooth by their chart formulas. Thus $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric with $q^*g=\hat g$; this identity also uniquely determines $g$, since $q$ is onto and $dq_p$ is invertible. Furthermore $g(N,N)_{q(p)}=\hat g(\hat N,\hat N)_p=-1$, so $N$ is a time orientation.

(The closed curve.) The curve $\hat\sigma(s):=x^{-1}(s,0,0,0)$ on $[0,L]$ is smooth and satisfies $\hat\sigma(L)=x^{-1}(L,0,0,0)=1\cdot\hat\sigma(0)$. Hence $\sigma=q\circ\hat\sigma$ is smooth and $\sigma(L)=q(1\cdot\hat\sigma(0))=\sigma(0)$. Its tangent is $\sigma'(s)=dq_{\hat\sigma(s)}(\partial_0)\neq0$ by step 2.1, and step 3.1 gives $g(\sigma',\sigma')=-1$ and $g(N,\sigma')=-1$. Thus $\sigma$ is future timelike and nonconstant with coincident endpoints.

(Flatness.) Let $r\in M$ and $p\in q^{-1}(r)$. Since $q$ is a local diffeomorphism there are open neighborhoods $\hat U$ of $p$ and $V$ of $r$ with $q|_{\hat U}:\hat U\to V$ a diffeomorphism; let $s:V\to\hat U$ be its inverse and $u:=x\circ s:V\to\mathbb R^4$ the induced chart ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). For $r'\in V$ and $v,w\in T_{r'}M$ one has $g_{r'}(v,w)=\hat g_{s(r')}(ds_{r'}v,ds_{r'}w)$ by $q^*g=\hat g$ from step 3.1. In the induced chart $u=x\circ s$, $ds$ takes each coordinate basis vector to the corresponding $x$-coordinate basis vector; hence $g_{ab}=\hat g_{ab}\circ s=\eta_{ab}$, constant by [L1] and [L5]. By [L6] the Christoffel symbols of the metric-selected connection vanish identically in this chart, and then the curvature formula of [L4] gives $R^a{}_{bcd}(r)=0$. As $r\in M$ was arbitrary and vanishing of a tensor at a point is chart-independent, $R\equiv0$ on $M$. The same charts exhibit for each point a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of Minkowski space, in accordance with clause (d) of [[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]].

(No global isometry.) Suppose $F:M\to\mathbb R^4$ satisfies $F^*\eta=g$. Let $f:=(F\circ\sigma)^0=x^0\circ F\circ\sigma$; $f$ is smooth by [L5], so continuous on $[0,L]$ and differentiable on $(0,L)$, with $f(L)-f(0)=0$ because $\sigma(L)=\sigma(0)$. By [L7] there is $c\in(0,L)$ with $f'(c)=0$. On the other hand, for every $s$, [L8] and step 4.1 give $\eta\bigl((F\circ\sigma)'(s),(F\circ\sigma)'(s)\bigr)=g(\sigma'(s),\sigma'(s))=-1$, that is
$$-\bigl(f'(s)\bigr)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl((F\circ\sigma)^i\bigr)'(s)^2=-1,$$
so $\bigl(f'(s)\bigr)^2=1+\sum_{i=1}^3((F\circ\sigma)^i)'(s)^2\ge1$ and $f'(s)\neq0$; in particular $f'(c)\neq0$, a contradiction. Hence no such $F$ exists. Since a global chart $u$ with $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$ constant would make $u$ an isometry onto its image (with $\eta$ given by those constants), no such chart exists either.

(Conclusion.) Steps 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 4.2 produce a connected time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ with $R\equiv0$ and a nonconstant closed future timelike curve; step 5.1 shows it is not isometric to Minkowski space and admits no global chart with constant components $\eta_{ab}$. This refutes the statement; the local isometry statement of [[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] is not contradicted but is precisely local, as its clause (d) asserts. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1] ∎



- **Local versus global.** The example isolates the topological obstruction to the converse of the local flatness theorem: vanishing curvature gives locally constant-component charts but does not prevent a compact timelike direction, which produces closed timelike curves and defeats the global argument in step 5.1 (the real-valued function $f$ on the circle direction cannot be strictly increasing). The construction is purely mathematical: no matter, observer, clock or measurement occurs.
- **Related models.** Other identification patterns of the flat model give flat manifolds with different global properties (for example identifications by spacelike translations, as in the flat torus). The specific timelike identification here is the one for which the closed curve is timelike; a spacelike identification instead yields closed spacelike curves and no closed causal curve.

boundaries.reason: The quotient manifold M and the interval [0,L] are nonempty; the compact sets used in properness are arbitrary but no empty case is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 disposes of the trivial group element n = 0 in freeness, and step 4.1 uses η(∂0,∂0) = -1 ≠ 0 while the tangent σ' is nowhere zero because dq is injective; the zero-velocity degenerate case cannot occur.

boundaries.reason: All objects are four-dimensional; no one-dimensional case is claimed.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 verifies that the action is free (trivial stabilizers) and proper, which excludes the degenerate non-free cases; the metric descended in step 4.1 is nondegenerate Lorentzian by the explicit descent argument in step 3.1.
step 4.1 closes the curve at the endpoints σ(0) = σ(L) via the group element 1 ∈ ℤ, and step 5.1 applies the mean value theorem on the closed interval [0,L], covering both endpoints.

step 1.1 verifies properness of the ℤ-action by bounding |n|L in terms of the compact sets K1, K2, so the finiteness of the relevant set of group elements is established by an explicit bound rather than by a choice principle.

boundaries.reason: The counterexample refutes the implication 'flat implies globally Minkowski'; it asserts no equivalence.
The converse (Minkowski is flat) is not in question and is not used.

risk_review.notes: Verified free discrete timelike translations: L>0 gives trivial stabilizers, compact coordinate bounds give finitely many translating integers, and each preimage piece is closed in compact domain. Free proper quotient has dimension four and submersion hence invertible dq. Metric and time orientation descend independently of representative via q composition identity. Local inverse charts retain eta, so curvature zero. Closed future timelike sigma has norm -1; any smooth eta-pullback map forces |f prime|>=1, while coincident endpoints force a zero derivative by Rolle. This also excludes a global constant-component chart onto any open image. No additional choice beyond the geometry suppliers inherited AC_omega is used.
